# The Eleventh House
<margin>11</margin>

The Eleventh House is placed <gloss>it is also called</gloss> the eleventh house and is known as the house of hope, confidence, and praise. It also concerns counselors, supporters, and those who increase one’s status, and it signifies the middle way of trust. The first lord of the <term>triplicity</term> <note>A group of three zodiac signs belonging to the same element (Fire, Earth, Air, or Water); each triplicity is ruled by three specific planets.</note> of the house of confidence signifies trust; the second signifies riches; the third signifies distinction or excellence.

Regarding this, we should speak with certainty about the parts. The house and its lord, measured in the region, signify what will happen to one’s counselors and their reliability regarding evil or the contrary. If it looks toward the middle parts at that time—as **Haly** <note>Haly Abenragel, a medieval Arabic astrologer whose "Complete Book on the Judgment of the Stars" was a standard textbook.</note> says in the third and fourth sections—see where it meets above the Tenth House. [If the lord] is found fortunate and strong in its position and in its proper place, it signifies faith and equality. If it is impeded, it is harmful to the counselors.

If the first lord of the triplicity, as **Haly** says, is in its own <term>bounds</term> <note>Subdivisions of a zodiac sign where a specific planet has additional influence.</note> and is fortunate and strong, judge that the person born <note>The "natus" or subject of the birth chart.</note> will have many friends, good fortune, and confidence. But if the lord of the triplicity is unfortunate and afflicted, the person will be neglected by others, having no one to turn to for help, and will be alienated from those they thought were friends or associates.

If the second lord of the triplicity is fortunate and well-placed, the person will be lucky, honored by lords, and will abound in good deeds and a good livelihood. But if this lord is afflicted, the person will be hardworking but will eventually fall into poverty and manifest misery.

If the third lord of the triplicity is fortunate and strong, the person will have children and will be a master in their realm after their father’s time, possessing good status and fortune. But if it is unfortunate and weak, the person will not have children, or if they do, the heirs will be in a worse state than their parents. After the lord of the <term>ascendant</term> <note>The sign rising on the eastern horizon at the moment of birth.</note>, look to the lord in the Eleventh House; if it is in a good place relative to the ascendant and in a good part of the triplicity, then the person will have love and gravity from powerful people and friends.

---

# The Twelfth House
<margin>12</margin>

The Twelfth House signifies enmities, labors, and sorrows. It also signifies misfortunes, great animals <note>Often referring to livestock or "beasts of burden" in traditional astrology.</note> that are captured, and hidden enemies. Regarding the lords: the first lord of the triplicity of this house signifies enemies; the second signifies labor; the third signifies large beasts.

**Haly Abenragel** says in his instructions: look at the lord of the triplicity of this house. If it is found to be fortunate and strong in some way, judge that the person’s enemies will not be able to overcome them, and the person will do with the enemy as they wish. But if the lord is <term>cadent</term> <note>Located in a house that "falls away" from the main angles of the chart, often weakening the planet's power.</note>, afflicted, and weak, the person will be under the power of their enemies, who will hinder them and bring them the evil they intended for the subject.

If the second lord of the house is fortunate, the person will have moderate fortune and property. If it is afflicted, there will be much death and sorrow, and they will suffer from labor, impediments, and great damage, remaining in a sluggish state.

If the third lord of the house is fortunate, the person will be eloquent, well-spoken, and happy in their fields and lands, with others helping them in their works. But if it is afflicted, they will be hindered and will have no remedy against their adversaries and those who wish them ill.

---

# Colors of the Houses
<margin>Colors of the Houses</margin>

It should be known that the twelve houses have colors according to their sections. For the proper color:
The 1st house is **white**.
The 2nd house is **green**.
The 3rd house is **saffron** (yellow).
The 4th house is **red**.
The 5th house is **honey-colored**.
The 6th house is **black**.

<margin>
Power; here the planets have their joys in whichever of the houses.
</margin>

Regarding the planets, they also have positions in the houses where their power is increased, which is called their **joy**. 
The **Moon** rejoices in the 3rd house.
**Venus** rejoices in the 5th house.
**Mercury** rejoices in the 6th house.
The **Sun** rejoices in the 9th house.
**Jupiter** rejoices in the 11th house.
**Saturn** rejoices in the 12th house.
The **Ascendant** (1st house) signifies fortune and perfection. Houses that are "falling" <note>Cadent houses.</note> signify debility. When the lord is in the first house, it signifies discovery and public fame. Thus you shall judge.

# Concerning the Joys of the Planets and the Houses

Therefore, all joys and intentions <unclear>intentions</unclear> were led by this logic. For the Sun joys in the 9th house, while the Moon joys in the 3rd. The 12th and 6th houses signify charity through <unclear>distant</unclear> <term>aspects</term> <note>The geometric angles between planets; "charity" here likely refers to the "benefic" or helpful influence of certain planetary placements.</note>. Likewise, if the lords of the **angular houses** <note>original: "angulis"; the 1st, 4th, 7th, and 10th houses, which are the most powerful points in a chart.</note> are found in all the houses, particularly the lord of the 2nd and the lords of the angles themselves, they signify a magnitude of honor and power; they shall be praised by both chance and fortune. However, the presence of these lords in **cadent houses** <note>original: "cadentibus"; the 3rd, 6th, 9th, and 12th houses, traditionally considered weaker or "falling away."</note> from the angles signifies loss and disgrace by misfortune.

The 11th house, which succeeds the 10th, and its lord signify a middle fortune—that is, they signify a fortune that is not as great as the 10th. The 9th house, which succeeds the 8th, signifies a middle fortune through gifts, commerce, and the affection of children. The 2nd house and its lord signify middle fortune on the part of servants and helpers. The 8th house and its lord signify middle fortune regarding inheritances and deaths <unclear>shortly</unclear> through all the significations of the lords of the angles when they are present in those angles. 

They signify the presence of a lord openly shown, and signify fortune with <unclear>power</unclear> through the kingdom or through acquisition. If [the lord] is in the 8th, it signifies acquisition through <unclear>disputes</unclear>; if it is in the 10th, it signifies acquisition through masteries or offices; if it is in the 2nd, it signifies acquisition through inheritances, and from that part it is through gifts <unclear>water</unclear> <unclear>land</unclear>. In the 10th and 11th houses, there are fortunes through a king and a great ruler and through high masteries. If it is in the 9th, it signifies <unclear>profit</unclear> through land protection or through the <unclear>king</unclear>. If it is in the 8th, it signifies <unclear>profit</unclear> through the king's ministers, the cultivation of the earth, the building of a city, the <unclear>reduction</unclear> of a deed, and through the guarding of a city.

If it is in the 7th, it signifies <unclear>profit</unclear> through the house in the <unclear>middle</unclear> and privacy of the house from the goods of the lord's <unclear>property</unclear>. In the 1st house, it signifies fortune through negotiations, land, and commendations, and through the <unclear>hand</unclear> of a <unclear>sower</unclear>. If it is in the 2nd, it signifies fortune through <unclear>disputes</unclear> and negotiations, and through land, inheritance, and the cultivation of the earth. If it is in the <term>ascendant</term> <note>The zodiac sign rising on the eastern horizon at the moment of birth.</note>, it signifies fortune through negotiations and middle-level business, and through astronomy <note>original: "asenomie"; likely meaning astrology in this context.</note> and through hope <unclear>provided</unclear> in general and the gift of a daughter. 

If it is present in the 10th, it signifies fortune through inquiries and negotiations on behalf of kings and through the land of the kingdom. The presence of the lord in the 12th or 2nd house signifies fortune from the fruit of the land, whether new or <unclear>ancient</unclear>. If it is present in the ascendant, it signifies fortune from the cultivation of the earth and its fruit, and <unclear>profit</unclear> from the king in general. If it is present in the 10th, it signifies a presence from the king’s <unclear>property</unclear> and fruit through masters. If it is present in the 8th, it signifies fortune from the cultivation of the earth and fruit, from a <unclear>great</unclear> <unclear>profit</unclear> and through land and <unclear>everything</unclear>. Thus, concerning the entry of the lords, it signifies that when the lords of the angles are present in the angles themselves, it is as was said of the angles <unclear>not</unclear> under the names of the lords, for it is so in all houses, and since the same applies to two of the angles, it applies to all.

<margin>To know the ruling planet</margin>
In another <unclear>way</unclear>: when you wish to know the ruling planet in this <unclear>matter</unclear>, choose the significator for the matter in two parts. First, look to the 2nd house, in which the <unclear>king</unclear> <unclear>is</unclear> the significator. Second, we ought to look to the planet which signifies <unclear>all</unclear> things. To do this, we must look to the 2nd house, which is the house of <term>substance</term> <note>A traditional term for personal wealth and moveable property.</note>, and with this, we must look to the nature of the thing signified. If it concerns <unclear>money</unclear>, we must look to <unclear>where</unclear> the significator is, or for any other matter of the houses and planets. 

However, in this matter, we must hold the planet we choose on behalf of the house as the present significator. The planet that signifies the nature of the matter is the one we must use. When you wish to know the ruling planet of the significators, look to which planet has the most **fortitude** <note>original: "fortitudine"; the combined strength of a planet based on its position, sign, and relationships to other planets.</note> in the house and in all its strengths, as found in the chapter on the fortitudes of planets in their <term>dignities</term>. The one who abounds in all fortitude, he is the leader of the significators.

Who is the **significator** <term>significator: the planet that represents the person asking a question or the specific topic being analyzed</term> in a question? First, if one asks according to the **house** <note>original: "domum"; one of the twelve divisions of the sky in a chart</note>, the first is the [lord of the house]. If one asks according to the state through the columns [of the table], it is said that the strength of the planets depends on their positions. For example, regarding the house and the gift of the house: Mercury has in Mercury <unclear>certain</unclear> fortitude, and the Sun is exalted. The Sun has 7 points of fortitude. And the lord of the Moon <note>original: "lha", likely an abbreviation for Luna</note> and the retrograde parts are implicated; the lord of the Moon has 3 points of fortitude in this position. It is in the 2nd fortitude, which is the **face** <term>face: a minor planetary dignity covering ten degrees of a zodiac sign</term> of Mercury. In its own fortitude, the Sun has 3 [points]. Where the Sun has the most fortitude, it holds the lordship. Therefore, one must have full fortitude to be the significator.

<margin>Concerning the dignities and attributes of the planets</margin>
Where it appears that the dignities are known through the table, some are through the [planet's] generation and others through their **dignities** <term>dignity: the "strength" a planet gains by being in a specific part of the zodiac, such as its Domicile or Exaltation</term> among the other planets. This difference of dignity is recognized through whether the planet is by day or by night. There is one natural dignity of the planets which is called their "honor." And this is so, as it appears they rule either in the day or in the night; some are of the day, some are of the night. If the question is by day, [the day planet rules]; if by night, the night planet. Furthermore, planets are figured as **masculine** and **feminine**; and the retrograde is feminine. When a planet is in its own "honor"—that is, in its natural slow motion—it is then in its own strength, just as a lord is in his own place. This is explained according to the introduction of **Alchabitius** <note>Alchabitius (d. 967) was a famous Arab astrologer whose "Introduction to the Art of Judgments" was a standard textbook in Medieval Europe.</note> to the master, and through the light which the investigator compares to the figure through the parts of the page.

<margin>The differences in the nature of the planets</margin>
The distinct natures of the planets are noted here. First, one distinguishes the nature according to the qualities of the planets. Second, one distinguishes the order according to the movement of the planets in the heavens. Third, concerning the nature of the **Dragon's Head and Tail** <term>Dragon's Head and Tail: the Lunar Nodes (Rahu and Ketu), where the Moon's path crosses the Sun's path</term>. Fourth, one distinguishes the order of the planets as they are above or below. The parts correspond to the nature of the stars: 1. In the judgment of the soul; 2. In the limbs of the body; 3. In the years of life; 4. In the Sun; 5. In the Moon. These parts respond to the nature of fate and signify the dispositions of men. This is compared to the order of the **aspects** <note>original: "aspct"; the geometric angles between planets that determine their relationship</note> of the Moon toward those parts of cold love, which are also understood through the nature of fate.

<margin>The Firdaria of Aries</margin>
Consider the **Firdaria** <term>Firdaria: a system of planetary periods where different planets "rule" certain spans of a person's life</term> which in a divine nativity are assigned. The Sun governs for 10 years, followed by the others in their order, such as the Moon governing its time. This distribution of years allows for the judgment of the planets and their nature throughout the differences of the human lifespan. This is the great secret of the ancestors, understood by the greatest intellects concerning the foundations of the planetary order.

<margin>Concerning Saturn</margin>
I speak now of **Saturn**. You should understand this planet as the first among the others. It signifies the nature of the mind and the greatest strength over fate and flight. It is attributed a medium fortitude. This is the expression of the question given in the tables for the study of its coldness and darkness. **Albumasar** <note>Albumasar (787–886 AD) was a Persian astrologer whose works were central to the recovery of Aristotle in the West.</note> says that this planet represents ancient things, deep things, and fixed foundations. **Haly** <note>likely Haly Abenragel, an 11th-century Arab astrologer</note> says that it signifies the father and the elders. It is cold and dry, signifying heavy labor and things of the earth. When it is in a bad state, it signifies malice, sadness, and hatred. Because of its coldness, it is associated with the color black and with things that remain hidden or are slow to change. It is the planet of old age and of those who work the land. In the figure of the world, it is the most distant and the slowest, governing the mutation of times and the foundations of buildings. It is the lord of memory and of things that are long-lasting.

We are able to understand the virtues of the stars, which does not require [further proof]. If a man forgets himself and listens, it is said that the works of the bodies of the **Sun** and **Moon** appear more clearly than the works of other stars; the work of those stars is much more manifest because of their abundance and their proximity to the stars that possess virtue. This proximity is felt in the individual souls of living beings and in their physical substances. But we remain influenced by them through that which is above us, not just once but many times, and if the mind follows a single material throughout the sphere, it will attain virtue in this way.

**Haly Abenragel** <note>Albohazen Haly (Ali ibn Abi al-Rijal), an 11th-century Arab astrologer whose work *De iudiciis astrorum* was a standard medieval text.</note> says regarding the nature of **Saturn**: it is a reddish planet, large, weary, and lowly, but with an anxiety and tepidness. Its nature is cold and dry, and it assists the **melancholic** <term>melancholic: one of the four humors, associated with the element of earth, coldness, and dryness</term> humor which lies beneath it. No one who has been under its influence admits of its nature, for it possesses the nature of both the earth and the land together; all things are led forth in its form and disposition, so that from its perfect and marvelous perfection, one will see and hear it speak of things. **Alfraganus** <note>Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Kathir al-Farghani, a 9th-century astronomer known for his *Elements of Astronomy*.</note> says that the body of Saturn is 90 times the size of the Earth.

<margin>2</margin>
**Jupiter** is a masculine fortune; it has a good nature that brings all things on Earth to [perfection]. **Ptolemy** <note>Claudius Ptolemy, the 2nd-century author of the *Tetrabiblos*, the foundational text of Western astrology.</note> says that its virtue leads to glorious things on the earth, and its place in the middle [of the spheres] brings a balanced heat; for this reason, its virtue heats and moistens. Haly says in the commentary of the prologue that its [virtues] give life to living things. It is said that the work of the stars follows the form of opinion concerning them; for if they are moist in virtue, all other things will be made [likewise]. This virtue is not something lowly, but it is seen through others as a hindrance to us. Therefore, I say that if the work of the stars is according to nature, they are like princes; those who are evil in virtue have confidence divided from one part of the orb to the other.

Before all else, if all celestial bodies have such a temperament—being heavy and dry—then the planet **Saturn**, in its own temperament, consists of the nature of the earth. Because of this, it has a determined **aspect** <term>aspect: the specific angular relationship between two planets, thought to change their influence</term> for many reasons; they are dried out by it. But if we see what the virtues of the stars are, and assume that others exist in whatever division is under the planets, their work and the space of the lands is more safely preserved through the mediation of coldness than by the great heat which consumes everything. But **Alfraganus** says that it [Jupiter] heats and moistens.

**Haly Abenragel** says: **Mars** is a planet of heat which corrupts while [other] stars are improving things; it passes over the lands because of its physical association.

<margin>1</margin>
[Mars] acts with improvement toward their perfection and [the removal of] deficiencies. Alfraganus says it is a natural planet, and one should not abhor Saturn for its nature; for when the time of the world’s earth was established, it was in the house of Light in **Aries**, **Taurus**, and **Gemini**; it diminished in its own [influence], but in **Leo** and **Virgo** it obtained [power]; in **Libra**, **Scorpio**, and **Sagittarius** it stood firm; it was blocked in **Capricorn**, **Aquarius**, and **Pisces**. Alfraganus says that the body of Jupiter is 94 times the size of the Earth.

**Mars** is masculine and harmful to our nature and our fathers; it dries things out, and because of its nature, it governs the body with a fiery color and the works of the planet; for this reason, the door is open beneath them. Haly says in the commentary to the prologue that the virtue of Mars is great, for it corrupts through itself, just as the image [suggests] that the works of Mars abound in their fiery color. I say that it is easy to see if they are to be diminished by the elements in the body of the earth; it is not in the water that changes the heat of people, but in particular, it teaches us regarding the proximity and distance in the sphere of the virtue of the stars, which we cannot fully understand. We can determine them by color, but if anyone doubts what we see of the work of the nature of Mars, [know that] the heat does not show itself in virtue through human ideas in earthly things—the ancient elements—for in the heavens it is not so. There is nothing lowly in the opposing element of water because it yields to the virtue of other planets in a direct line; but its virtue is through that which is done by the Sun; much is given because it happens that much is revealed in that body.

The **Luminaries** <note>The Sun and Moon</note> have their rising in the 10th sign from the Sun. At that time, they are said to be 10 degrees from the Sun in the eastern part, or at night in a <term>trine</term><note>An aspect where two celestial bodies are 120 degrees apart.</note> from the Moon. Then, truly in an <term>angle</term><note>A cardinal point or significant angular relationship.</note> from the Moon through conjunction, they are then said to be in their **dignity** <note>A state of astrological strength or essential power.</note>.

The angle called "opposition" has no place here, because a planet joined in opposition to the first [the Sun] and the Moon is [initially] more eastern or western than them. Afterward, it is said that every planet is "polluted" by their rays from the Earth, for then it appears from the conjunction in governed time. Those within 12 degrees of the Sun’s rays are called **oppressed** <note>original: "oppressi"; often referred to as "combust," meaning the planet's influence is hidden by the Sun's glare.</note>. But when they are in the center of the Sun’s body (degree for degree) and are in the middle of the Sun's body, the "pollution" is removed from them because the planet's <term>latitude</term><note>The distance of a planet north or south of the ecliptic.</note> ends its motion and they are seen in the middle of the Sun's body <note>This specific state is known as "Cazimi," or being in the heart of the Sun, which was traditionally thought to strengthen a planet immensely rather than weaken it.</note>. 

Afterward, this motion is said to be in any conjunction or from **retrograde** motion through the mastery of the pole. Regarding the three "higher" planets <note>Mars, Jupiter, and Saturn</note>, it speaks of being "eastern." A planet is called eastern when it emerges from under the Sun's rays; then it first appears in the morning at sunrise, moving away from the Sun's longitude. They pertain to eastern boundaries, and since the Sun is ahead at midnight, they are then called "western from the right." They are called **eastern** when they follow the lordship at sunrise. 

Conversely, it is said that "eastern" is more on the right side than the Sun. Let us place ourselves for this part with our face toward the world: what is at the rising is to the eastern left, having the right [on the other side]. Since from this even the higher planets can be said to be entirely on the left, it does not mean they are [only] in the eastern part. Within the first 21 degrees from the Sun, they are "right," and through the third part of the Sun, planets are on the left because they are in the western part from the Sun. 

Therefore, by lordship, every higher planet's <term>epicycle</term><note>In pre-Copernican astronomy, a small circle whose center moves around the circumference of a larger circle (the deferent).</note> is at a degree where it confers with the planet in the middle of the Earth's rays. When a planet is distant from the Sun so that it is seen in the morning before sunrise, it is called **eastern**. Then its lordship is governed by the Sun and the pole in the upper part of the epicycle. In this space, they have a distance from the Sun... therefore they can then be called "left." 

When they emerge from under the Sun's rays, they are western and greatly increase in **strength**. When they are distant from the Sun by 30 to 90 degrees, they are called **strong** because of their distance. They are called "eastern" as they move toward weakness. Afterward, as they move away from the planet more quickly toward the Sun's opposite, they are called "eastern" in degrees through the opposition... after this, they are "eastern strong" within 30 degrees. They are called "rejoicing" <note>original: "gaudentes"</note> at the planet's weakness and "eastern weak" when governed thus. 

Furthermore, when they are at a distance from the Sun in body, they are eastern and called "weak" as they move toward the lordship's boundary. When far from the Sun in **opposition**, and in **retrograde** motion, they are "eastern strong." But they become "eastern weak" when oppressed by the Sun's rays near conjunction. 

Some say the logic is false, since it is not possible for them to be 60 degrees from the Sun in 30 parts... many degrees of the body are seen in their own lines, moving away from the Sun more quickly. This happens to planets in their removal... they can be seen in so many parts.

<meta>Continuing from page 115, which discussed the "transfer of light" and the movement of the Moon in relation to Saturn, Jupiter, and Mars. <margin>Regarding **restraint** <note>original: "refrenacio"</note></margin>

Next follows **abrenez** <note>original: "abrenez," likely a corruption of the Arabic term *al-inkifaf*, meaning a planet "refraining" from an aspect</note>, that is, **restraint**. It is said to occur when a planet wishes to be joined to a superior planet, but before it completes the application to the degree, it turns back <note>becomes retrograde</note>. For this reason, it is called "restraint."

For example: I suppose that **Saturn** is in the 20th degree. The **Sun** is in [a certain] degree and is coming toward **Saturn**. But before it reaches it, the **Sun** reaches its 18th degree, and then, before they can touch, **Saturn** begins to move away or the **Sun** begins to "refrain" <note>original: "frinat," meaning to pull back like a horse with a bridle</note>. In such a case, the **Sun** is said to be restrained, and it will not join with **Saturn**. This is understood both for application <note>moving toward</note> and for the moment before they unite, when a planet is suddenly found to be retreating.

This is also called **alacranda** <note>another likely Arabic derivative term</note>, which is said when two planets are in one sign, of which one is **heavier** <note>original: "ponderosior," referring to a slower-moving planet like Saturn or Jupiter</note> and the other is **lighter** <note>faster-moving, like Venus or Mercury</note>. Then, when the lighter one seeks the heavier one, but before they can join, the heavier one moves or the lighter one retreats, it is said to "refrain" from the aforementioned lighter one.

Example: I suppose that **Saturn** is in the 8th degree of **Aries** and **Jupiter** is in the 12th degree of **Aries**. **Jupiter**, being faster, seeks a union with **Saturn**. But before they join, **Mars** <note>original shorthand "mres"</note> retreats, and thus the union does not occur; it is held back and the position is lost. In this case, **Mars** descends and **Jupiter** does not fulfill its goal.

Another rule: **Fricitas** <note>original: "frrictas," likely "fraustratio" or frustration</note> occurs when a lighter planet comes toward a heavier one, but before they can join, the heavier one enters another sign. In that case, it "falls away" into another part. For when the lighter planet reaches the degree where the heavier one was, the heavier one has already moved into the next sign, and thus the first influence is annulled.

Example: **Jupiter** is in the 29th degree of **Leo**, and **Mars** is in the 24th degree, seeking **Saturn**. But before **Mars** can reach **Saturn**, it turns back. In this case, it falls out of **Leo**, and the influence of **Saturn** is annulled.

Now, concerning **the cutting off of light** <note>original: "abscisio luminis"</note>. This is when two planets—a lighter one seeking a heavier one—are in a sign, but from the sign of the heavier one comes another planet which reaches the lighter one first. In such a case, that intervening planet is said to "cut off the light" of the heavier planet from the planet that desired it. This differs from "refraint" because in that case a planet retreats, whereas here, another planet simply intercepts the influence.

This "cutting off of light" also happens when a lighter planet seeks a heavier one, and that heavier one is itself seeking another even heavier planet. For example: **Mars** seeks **Jupiter**, and **Jupiter** seeks **Saturn**. But before **Mars** reaches **Jupiter**, **Jupiter** reaches **Saturn**. In such a case, **Saturn** cuts off the light of **Jupiter** from **Mars**.

It is said here that one should note in which parts planets are **strengthened** and in which they are **weakened**.
First, they are strengthened by being near **Venus** and **Jupiter**, the "benefics." **Saturn** is strengthened when it is with the **Sun**. It is also understood that when a planet is in the same sign as another, it is in a strong position. If it is in an **angle** <note>The 1st, 4th, 7th, or 10th houses of an astrological chart, considered the most powerful locations</note>, it is very strong. If **Venus** is there, or if **Saturn** is in the 12th house, it is weakened. Thus, a planet can be carried from a position of strength to one of weakness or vice-versa. This is called "generation."

Furthermore, **Mars** is strengthened when it is in the same degree as **Jupiter** or **Saturn**. Light is also increased when a planet is in its "face" <note>A specific 10-degree subdivision of a zodiac sign</note> or in its "joy." **Mars** is said to be strong when it is retreating from the Sun's beams.
Planets are also fortified when they are in their **exaltation** <note>A specific sign where a planet's influence is heightened</note>. A masculine planet is strengthened in a masculine sign (like **Aries** or **Libra**), and a feminine planet in a feminine sign.
A planet is also strengthened by its location: if it is in a masculine sign by day, or a feminine sign by night. Finally, regarding the **malefics** <note>unlucky planets, usually Saturn and Mars</note>: they are strengthened or weakened based on their aspects. If the **Moon** applies to a malefic, it brings ill fortune unless it is corrected by the rays of a benefic.

# 6. The Great Conjunctions

The first [topic] concerns the **Great Conjunction** <note>original: "pma magna," referring to the *Coniunctio Magna* of Jupiter and Saturn, which medieval astrologers believed signaled major historical shifts</note> of all types. Some of these are very specific and return [to the starting point] every **960 years**. This shift occurs once every **240 years**, which happens when the first conjunction reaches the **Water triplicity** before it completes its twelfth conjunction. 

The eighth [type] for every group is made when it is in the third triplicity. This occurred in its cycle on a day in the **year 1324**. From that time, for 20 years, [the conjunction] was in the same [triplicity]. In 1324, the conjunction was in **Aquarius**; after that, for 20 years, the conjunction is in **Libra**, and afterwards in **Gemini**. It continues in this order until the end of this term, having occurred twelve times. 

If you multiply 12 by 20, you find **240 years**, through which the shift will be changed. This is the "active" triplicity, meaning all things are changed through these matters. You should understand this through the other ten triplicities <note>likely referring to smaller sub-cycles</note>, just as the first great cycle returns to the start every 960 years. 

1. To the **Fire triplicity**: although the time of moving from one triplicity to another does not terminate at the very beginning of the 960 years, the time will remain under that triplicity for 120 [years] <note>The text here seems to discuss sub-divisions of the 240-year shift</note>. 

The shift is dangerous, because 240 tripled makes 720, and adding the final part makes 960. The time of the whole heart <note>perhaps referring to the core of the cycle</note> returns to the first [point] at the beginning of this heritage of the triplicity. 

### Sub-divisions of Conjunctions

*   **11. The third [type]:** which is made immediately in the [signs?], which occurs every **20 years**.

These are all great signs; others are counted in years for the common people, which is 120, according to the reasoning of the seven [planets] which the **Chaldeans** <note>ancient Babylonian astrologers</note> promised.

### On the <term>Alchochode</term>, as taught in the [previous] chapter; how to choose the <term>Alchochode</term>, which is the **giver of the years of life**.

The summary then is this: when we wish to know which planet should be taken as the **giver of years** through the <term>Hyleg</term>, the <term>Hyleg</term> ought to be worthy of the highest fortune in the place of the <term>Hyleg</term>. And if it does not aspect [the Hyleg], one must look to the one after it, according to the planet it has.

...from the place up to the [Part of] Fortune, if there are not as many by the first method as there should be in the place up to Fortune, and it signifies then what is held through Fortune. Because of this, if it aspects the lord of the Term, he is positioned as the lord of the house. If this is not seen, the aspect is preferred. They say that if two or three or more planets share in the dignities so that they have equal dignity and fortune in the place of the Hyleg, and all aspect it, then that one should be taken which is closest [in degrees]. And if they are equal in this—which rarely happens—that one should be taken who was most praised by the ancients, such as the one who is the master of the circle, by one or two degrees. One should not be far from it. One should take the one who was closest to the **Angle** <term>Angle: The 1st, 4th, 7th, and 10th houses, which are the most powerful points in a chart.</term> and the one who was in the morning rising. Also, consider the one who was in aspect to **Mars** before the rising of the **Sun**, and the one who was in his own form returning to the common state, or the one who was praised in another place by the ancients, or who was occidental. And if he was in an angle, then he is superior; if he was occidental and of the nature of these [planets] which do not square, then he is the Hyleg. If he was in his house or in his exaltation, he is truly the Hyleg and the **Alchochoden**. And if he was the Hyleg but was in a cadent house <note>original: "cadente"; the 3rd, 6th, 9th, and 12th houses, considered the weakest because they "fall away" from the angles.</note>, he is still the Hyleg and Alchochoden, and one need not look for another in that point. Between the Alchochoden which is most powerful in the place of the Hyleg, let it be seen that it aspects it. But if none of the aforementioned conditions are met, then take both that give the Alchochoden. 

**Haly Abenragel** <note>Albohazen Haly Abenragel (965–1059 AD), an Arab astrologer whose "Book on the Skilled Physician" was a foundational text in medieval Europe.</note> gives a little more to the masters of the art to narrate. Haly Abenragel says that many of the wise have said that those who are Alchochodens in dignity give their **Greater Years**; those who are in succedent houses give their **Middle Years**; and those in cadent houses give their **Lesser Years**. This gives a better understanding, for to place one above the other otherwise is an error in the science of the Alchochoden. Let it be known that for the truth of the matter, the sign must be considered. 

When the Alchochoden ends in the 10th degree of the house, it gives its Greater Years; and when it ends in the 11th degree of the house, it gives its Middle Years. And when it is moved from one of these two places, the years do not aspect [the same way]. Whatever is between one and the other is divided between the greater years and the middle years. 

For example, if the 10th degree and 7th degree have passed, and the Alchochoden is in the 13th degree, it is elongated from the point. Therefore, for the 10th degree, it gives its Greater Years, which are 82. And if it were in the point of the 11th house, it would give its Middle Years, which are 49. The difference between these two points is 33 years <note>82 minus 49 is 33. The text's "24" and "31" seem to be part of a specific calculation or involve a transcription error in the numbers.</note>. By the distance of the planet from the point in the 10th house, which is 310, divided by 30... it results in 11 months. Through the third part, 12 years and 4 months are subtracted from the greater years, and there remain 60 years and 8 months. These are the years that the planet gives in such a case.

<meta>This page continues the technical instructions for determining the "gift of years" (life expectancy) provided by the Alchochoden (the Giver of Years). It specifically addresses how a planet’s proximity to the Sun (combustion) and its motion (retrograde or direct) increase or decrease the years it bestows upon the native.</meta>

<margin>folio 148</margin>
According to the angles and the other seven houses, **Haly Abenragel** <note>Abu l-Hasan 'Ali ibn Abi l-Rijjal (died c. 1037), a famous Arab astrologer whose work "The Complete Book on the Judgment of the Stars" was a standard textbook in medieval Europe.</note> states that the **Alchochoden** <term>Alchochoden: The planet that "gives" the number of years a person will live, based on its strength in the birth chart.</term> is misused when it is placed near the Sun, so that it does not appear or grant its whole gift <note>The "gift" (Latin: *datum*) refers to the specific number of years—Great, Middle, or Lesser—assigned to a planet.</note>; and if it does not thereafter grant the day and the hour. It is said that those who do not have this [strength] are as if in a state of **combustion** <term>Combustion: A planet is "combust" when it is too close to the Sun (usually within 8.5 to 15 degrees), which was thought to "burn up" its power and make it ineffective.</term>. Thus, if the planet suffers in its cause from the Sun, the Sun sends [influence] to it, and it ends between the angles. Thus, the ruler of the house is treated by the Sun, and it ends at 10 degrees.

If the planet is not in the [strength of] the day, it ends 14 degrees before the Sun rises; and the planet starts at 9 degrees. It rises and performs its function and gives its complete gift of years. The rulers are 9. By the house, it ends what was said of the house, but it does not appear for all days from the degrees by the rule in the true days at that point. It gives, however, not completely, but through the lord of the degrees, as it approaches the Sun within 14 degrees. From 4 degrees toward completion, it gives only a small amount because of its weakness. At [other] degrees, it gives its house completely. **Isidore** <note>Likely referring to Isidore of Seville, though he is less common in purely technical astrological texts than Haly.</note> says it does well when it appears near the Sun at the midpoint. 

At 4 degrees, it gives its whole house completely; but if it gives the whole when it applies to the Sun, going toward it, it ends at 14 degrees and is weakened with its half-gift, giving only a little—that is, 5 [years]. If it assists or applies to the Sun at 12 degrees, it gives the whole gift of the house. If the Sun is near 12 degrees, it gives a small gift of 8 [years], or it assists while crossing the Sun by 12 degrees, and then it will give the gift completely. 

The **Fall** <term>Fall: A position in the zodiac opposite a planet's "Exaltation" where it is considered weakest.</term> of a planet from its **Exaltation** <term>Exaltation: A specific sign where a planet is thought to be at its maximum strength.</term> takes away a portion of the gift. So the Sun, when it ends in 14 degrees, or 24 degrees, suffers in its fall by half. The judgment is similar regarding the diameter <note>original: "du_me_t_ru"; likely referring to the opposition aspect (180 degrees).</note>. The **Tail of the Dragon** <term>Tail of the Dragon (Cauda Draconis): The South Node of the Moon, traditionally considered a point of decrease or malific influence.</term> in its fall from 23 degrees gives the gift of the house through 20 degrees. The same figure is judged by the diameter. The planet in its fall from 20 degrees of Capricorn toward the completion of 20 degrees gives [less]; the same figure is judged by the diameter. If the lady of the house in her fall from 14 degrees goes with the strength to the end of her latitude, the same figure is judged by the diameter. 

And it is beneficial in its fall when crossing the house if at 21 degrees of Scorpio. Secondly, what is said regarding the intention of **Ptolemy** <note>Claudius Ptolemy, the 2nd-century author of the *Tetrabiblos*, the foundational text for Western astrology.</note> at 18 degrees, which we rule according to the positions and according to **Al-Abun** <note>Likely a corruption of an Arabic authority like Al-Buni or similar.</note>, and so there it ends in 12 degrees of Pisces. 

Thus, the text of **Haly** is corrupted. It is understood in the same way in the intention of Ptolemy. From my research, the fall is from 8 degrees of Pisces up to the completion of 19 degrees, and its deficiency is judged as if it were in its fall. Therefore, it has its gift in its own place from its **retrogradation** <term>Retrogradation: When a planet appears to move backward in the sky; usually considered a sign of weakness or delay.</term> toward the opposition of the Sun. Toward the middle of its retrogradation, it takes away half of the gift, and half remains. And because at the end of the opposition it may be more [distant], one must calculate the degrees from the opposition until it ends. 

One takes the portion proportional to 10 degrees if it is retrograde from the opposition toward the **direct** <term>Direct motion: When a planet moves forward again after being retrograde, regaining its strength.</term> motion. Then you should add half of the gift and direct your way in such a manner that the planet ends in the first [degree] of its direct motion. It will give its gift completely. 

For example, I pose that it was in a certain place and its gift of years was 60. But because it is retrograde, it loses half, so it loses 30 years. And I pose that it has lived through half of its retrogradation or the opposition of the Sun by 2 degrees. And I pose that from the opposition until the direct motion, it ought to be retrograde for 10 degrees. I will therefore multiply the 2 degrees by the half-gift it lost (which was 30), and it results in 60. I divide that 60 by the 10 degrees, which results in 6. Therefore, I add 6 years to the half-gift (the 30 years), and it results in 36 years. This is the gift within its portion. 

The lord of the [place] who follows the sign of the Scorpion, it can give half of its gift. First, compute its unity as the planets are positioned which appear very strong. So it is able to be judged in those degrees, so that if it does not fail there, it is through the mode of the degrees. Multiply the degrees which are avoided through the retrograde, and it will give the gift that remains. This is how one calculates the gift according to **Haly**.

Limits and that after the birth, one must choose the **Almuten** <term>Almuten: The planet that holds the most "dignity" or power over a specific point or the entire birth chart.</term> for duration and a blessed beginning. # Heart and Destiny

<meta>This page continues the technical exposition of astrological methods, shifting from planetary strengths to the specific calculation of the "Arabic Parts" or "Lots"—mathematical points on the zodiac derived from the distance between two planets and projected from the Ascendant. It draws heavily on the work of Abu Ma’shar (Albumasar), a preeminent Persian astrologer of the 9th century.</meta>

### Exposition and Distinction of Abu Ma’shar’s Introduction to the Mastery of Judgments of the Stars

The preface mentions those things omitted previously. The question is how to provide the book in which the previous predictions are found. I have divided it into two parts: the first part contains the **Parts** <note>original: "ptes"; these are the "Arabic Parts" or "Lots," which are specific mathematical points in a horoscope used to predict themes like wealth or marriage</note> that occur in **nativities** <note>a birth chart</note>; the second part contains the Parts that occur in the **revolutions of the years of the world** <note>mundane astrology, used to predict world events and the fate of nations</note>. With God's help, I have divided the first part into two sections: in the first, he gives the method of predicting the Parts in general and provides an example using the **Part of Fortune** <note>term: Part of Fortune (Pars Fortunae); a point representing worldly success and physical well-being</note>. In the second section, he places the specific Parts of the twelve **houses** <note>term: houses (domus); the 12 divisions of the sky representing different life areas like health, money, or travel</note>.

I will begin, therefore, with the Part of Fortune. According to the method of prediction, it has three primary modes. The first is to take the method of calculation, which is the distance between one specific place and another, and the total value that comes from that distance is added to another place. For example, if it is taken from one sign and then added above another [the Ascendant]. All signs are given 30 degrees, or 10 minutes, or [other values]... I posit that the Sun is at 6 degrees, and the Moon is at 12 degrees, and the **Ascendant** <note>the sign rising on the eastern horizon</note> is at 10 degrees. Thus, in the place of prediction, the calculation remains at 98 degrees, to which 10 degrees are added from the Ascendant, resulting in 108 degrees. Then, the Part is projected from that Ascendant, giving 30 degrees to each sign until it ends at 18 degrees of **Cancer** <note>original: "can̄i"</note>. This is the proposed position of the Part of Fortune.

<margin>Projection of the first Part</margin>
In the following section, he sets out the prediction of the Parts according to the order of the twelve houses, placing for each house the Parts belonging to it; and I have divided these into as many sections as there are houses.

<margin>Concerning the first Part</margin>
They begin with the Parts in the first house. First, he places the Part of the **Lord of the House** <note>the planet that rules the sign on the house’s cusp</note>... second is the Part of **Hyleg** <note>original: "vleg"; the planet that acts as the "giver of life" in a chart</note>; third is the Part of the master or sovereign; fourth is the Part of the lover and joy; fifth is the Part of stability and duration; sixth is the Part of spirit and audacity.

<margin>Concerning the first part: The Horoscope and Life</margin>
Again, concerning the Parts: take the Part of Life from the **Sun** to **Saturn** by day or by night, and project it from the Ascendant. **Abu Ma'shar** <note>original: "Albū ū"; 787–886 AD, one of the most influential astrologers in history</note> enters into our introduction to the mastery of the Parts, saying this is the Part of the end of the native's life, and it concerns whether they are long-lived or if they are planted in the dignity of the body and the joy of the day. And if there are few or many [degrees] in the aforementioned signs, they will arrive at the end.

<margin>The second part: Hyleg</margin>
Concerning the measurement... in the first... the Part of the **Hyleg** is taken from the Sun's degree or from the Ascendant in the nativity, or if the nativity was pre-natal; or from its ruler or the Ascendant. Abu Ma'shar says that this position designates the Hyleg through the degrees. He says that when it is directed toward the Hyleg, it will arrive at a good or bad end. **Many wise astrologers err** when they measure the length of a human life, or why they are not moved in certain times, because they do not consider the time according to the Hyleg and its arrival at the place of the "malefics" <note>harmful planets, usually Saturn or Mars</note>, which causes obstacles or unknown turns of events. Therefore, this was hidden from them because they did not direct this Part.

When they find a person to whom evil has happened, they begin with these signs of the aforementioned Parts. The **Part of Fortune** is taken in the day from the Moon to the Sun, and in the night from the Sun to the Moon, and projected from the Ascendant. Concerning the properties of this Part, Abu Ma'shar says it signifies the soul or the body and the condition of being; whether it is faith or religious devotion, or even the cultivation of God, or wealth, or hidden things, and everything that is absent or expected.

The second house has three Parts: the first is the Part of **Substance** [Wealth]; the second is the Part of money <note>original: "drachm̄"; drachmas</note>; the third is the Part of blessedness and victory. Abu Ma'shar says that the Part of Substance signifies food and drink by which bodies are sustained, and whether they are in a good place or not. The other Parts are those which are gathered and acquired... the significators of substance and the Part of Fortune.

<meta>This page continues the technical catalog of the "Arabic Parts" or "Lots," moving through the twelve astrological houses. <margin>+</margin> **The Third House** sets out the Parts of the 3rd house, and they are two. The first is the **Part of Brothers** <note>original: "pars fratrum"; refers to siblings in general</note>; the second is the **Part of Brotherly Benevolence** <note>the goodwill or harmony between siblings</note>. **Abu Ma’shar** <note>original: "Albusar"; a 9th-century Persian astrologer whose work was foundational to Western astrology</note> says regarding the Part of Brothers (under chapter 19.1) that the sign in which they fall indicates the siblings, their concord, and the love belonging to the native’s part and coming from them. He looks to see if it is under <margin>"</margin> them; if they fall in **signs of many children** <note>certain zodiac signs, like Pisces or Cancer, were traditionally thought to be "fruitful" or "prolific"</note>, siblings will be multiplied, and if they fall in **signs of few children**, they will be few. And if a **fortune** <note>term: fortune (fortuna); a benefic planet like Jupiter or Venus</note> or their ruler receives its ruler in the "fruit of the earth" <note>likely referring to a productive placement in the chart</note> and the ruler of the house in which it fell—and then the ruler of the Part from the same—you should assign the number of the sign according to the brother. If they are of the same sign, multiply the number of those signs. If they are from the father's side, take from the ruler of the house in which a planet fell. From all this, Abu Ma’shar sets one Part from this house <margin>comb</margin> <note>likely a shorthand for "combined" or a specific calculation</note> which is called the **Part of the Character of Brothers**. The 2nd Part is taken by day from the Sun to the degree of the **Midheaven** <note>original: "medii celi"; the highest point in the sky at the moment of birth</note>, and by night the reverse; and it shall be increased above the degree of the **Ascendant**. You shall know from their aspect how much time will be found for the Part to endure to signify the brothers; and as the sign of the year gives to each a degree of the day and hour, it will give to each the hour of the sign of the year and for each sign and proportional share, it owes an hour, and thus is it predicted from them.

**The Fourth House** sets out the Parts for the 4th house, and they are six. The first part is the **Part of the Father**; 2nd is the **Part of the Father’s Death**; 3rd is the **Part of Grandfathers**; 4th is the **Part of Inheritances and Possessions**; 5th is the **Part of the Native’s Nobility**; 6th is the **Part of Their Children**. This is for the day. For the Part of the Father's Death, take from the Sun to Saturn; for the Part of Inheritances and Possessions, from Saturn to Jupiter. The Part relating to the father indicates if they are good and of noble and fortunate standing; if they are **malefic** <note>original: "mali"; referring to "infortunes" like Mars or Saturn</note>, they are from those who are hardworking/laborious. From the Part of the Heir and the death of the native, he takes from the death and the condition of the father toward him, toward this Part or its present ruler, as is known and found by itself from these things for the sake of signification.

**The Fifth House** sets out the Parts of the 5th house, and they are four. The first is the **Part of Children**; 2nd is the **Part of the Father’s Sex** in which it is said "provided there are children"; 3rd is the Part in which **masculinity and femininity** are known; 4th is the Part by which one knows concerning the native about whom it is asked whether it be male or female. 4th, by which to know the Part, and you shall know the children. And if it is the Part of the Love of Children: the 1st is the Part of Children itself, and Abu Ma’shar says that if it is held in a sign of many children, he shall have many children; if it falls in a sign of few, he shall have few children. If it falls in a sign of few children, he shall have few children <note>the scribe repeats this phrase for emphasis or by error</note>. And if the Part is such, there will be children; if they are **fortunate**, the children will live; if **unfortunate**, they will die.

**The Sixth House** sets out the Parts of the 6th house, and they are two. The first is the **Part of Infirmities** <note>term: azemena; specific degrees of the zodiac believed to cause physical defects or "crippling" ailments</note> and their weaknesses—specifically in some limb; 2nd is the **Part of Servants**. If the Part of Infirmities is joined with a **fortune** <note>a benefic planet</note>, the native will be healthy in his limbs; if it is in an **unfortunate** part, the native will have incurable diseases and blemishes on the body. In the limbs, these sicknesses will be signified from the place of the infortunes.

**The Seventh House** sets out the Parts for the 7th house, and they are four. The first part is the **Betrothal of Men**; 2nd is the **Part of the Betrothal of Women**, and this is taken in two ways; 3rd is the **Part of Delight and Pleasure**; and the **Part of Emancipation**. Whether the Part of Betrothal is found by **direction** <note>an astrological timing technique where planets are moved forward through the zodiac at a rate of one degree per year</note> to Jupiter and Venus, and so by others concerning betrothal; and therefore, let him find in what matter the time of betrothal occurs, because then you will know the betrothal will come to that part by direction, giving one year to each degree.

**The Eighth House** sets out the Parts of the 8th house, and they are four. The first part is for **Death**; 2nd is the **Part of Danger and Slaughter**; 3rd is the **Part of the Year** in which the native ought to die and of poverty; 4th is the **Part of the Benefactor and Legacies** <note>original: "promotoris et legatoris"; likely referring to executors of a will or those who leave bequests</note>. Abu Ma’shar says the 1st is the Part of Death, then by day from the Moon to <unclear>chapter 19.1</unclear>. And if they do not aspect them—that is, the native being killed by a most foul death—and if they do aspect, the strength will be changed. If the Moon alone aspects the Part, there will be a defense. And if the Part and the Moon are in the signs of "cut-off limbs," death looks toward him; if the Moon is **impeded** <note>term: impeded (impedita); a planet whose influence is weakened by a bad placement or a difficult connection to a malefic planet</note>, some of his limbs will be cut off. Or regarding the year in which death is feared because of the 2nd day, in which the **Lord of the Year** is impeded, the native shows much sickness and weariness in the body as well as health issues, and thus the whole is reached. And for the years, according to one degree of the sign, thus the year is known to reach this Part, and he finds the hour according to the completion and direction to the Ascendant and to...

<meta>This page continues the instructions for weather prediction (specifically rain) and transitions into a technical tutorial on how to use an almanac to calculate the exact time a planet enters a new zodiac sign. When the time for rain is at hand, take each day in the morning the distance from the position of the Sun to the position of Saturn;
if this distance is added to the position <note>The text implies adding this distance to the Moon's longitude to find the "Lot of Rain."</note>, and if it arrives at the degree <note>original: "azam" – likely a corruption of the Arabic word for degree or a specific part</note> of the Moon and the Moon aspects <note>term: aspect; a specific geometric angle between two celestial bodies that astrologers believe transmits influence</note> it, it sends rain. If it does not aspect it, there will only be clouds. And if it arrives in the house <note>term: house; here referring to the zodiac sign ruled by a planet</note> of Mercury, there will be wind; when in the house of Jupiter, winds! In the house of the Sun or Mars, it brings dryness instead of rain; when in the house of Venus, rain—if it is aspected by Venus from the Moon.
According to Plato <note>Likely referring to Plato of Tivoli, a 12th-century translator of Arabic astronomical texts</note>: you should count the hour when it is necessary to take the interval from the Moon, which is at the same hour as the position of the planets.
And if the Moon then is at the midpoint with Saturn and is itself retrograde <note>term: retrograde; the apparent backward motion of a planet in the sky</note> in a feminine sign, or if they are situated in an angle <note>term: angle; the four most powerful points in a horoscope: the Ascendant, Midheaven, Descendant, and Imum Coeli</note> of the ascendant at that hour, it is the opinion that rain will occur. When the third part follows, you must then understand the ascendant or the aspect in the house which is ascending and proceeding; there will be rain in such quantity as is in the judgment of the Moon between the ascendant and its power. Namely, those things which are founded upon the ascendant are certain. And if any of the aforementioned planets or the Moon is found in an angle of that ascendant at the time the weather began, there will be rain in that weather; when they are in common signs and not in an angle, it will not occur.

If you wish to have the entry of any planet into any sign, or wish to find a specific aspect, you must work as follows:
take from the Almanac the difference of the movement of the preceding day and the following day, and provide this difference first to the planet in your calculator table. And provide the degrees in the first place; then take the difference of the signs of the movement of that same preceding day—namely, from the beginning of the sign which the planet ought to enter—until the planet reaches the other sign, by subtracting the sign it is currently in from the previous difference; and all the way to the place of the center of those two signs, all the way to that sign for which you seek the hour of the planet's entry. And put this difference in the third place. When the differences are multiplied into minutes, with degrees and smaller degrees, the resulting product divided by the first number will be the hour of the planet's entry into the sign you seek. ∩

In the year of the Lord 1330. Beginning according to the mansions of the moon at 24 degrees <gloss>miles or measures</gloss>.
Subtract the degrees from the given place of the Moon, namely the degrees above 24. Divide the remainder by the number of one mansion, namely 12 degrees, 51 minutes, and 26 seconds; and you will find in which mansion the Moon was. And if at first you have the place of the Moon in the degrees above, it was in its own mansion. To that, add 24 degrees, and you will find the number of the mansion according to the teaching of Haly Abenragel <note>original: "haly abenagela"; Abu l-Hasan 'Ali ibn Abi l-Rijal, a 11th-century Arab astrologer whose "Book on the Fixed Stars" was a standard textbook</note> in the 8th book on elections <note>term: elections; the branch of astrology used to find the most auspicious time to begin an undertaking</note> regarding the lunar mansions, in the preface.

## On their good and bad days // Concerning good and bad hours for performing any action

For an hour in which to act without delay, look to the sign which will be in that day by the **points** <note>term: points (punctos); likely referring to "minutes" of a degree or specific numerical subdivisions used to calculate the exact position of a planet</note> that ascend then, and how many **degrees** and points are in that sign. Look at each point, and let the Moon be in the sign which will then be in the east, and observe every degree from the Sun even unto the Moon. Then you shall give 30 to the eastern sign, and to the other signs after it another 30, and where the sum ends, there is the good or bad hour for acting.

And if all were in masculine signs, there were the first signs of the east [signified by] the Sun in **Aries** <note>♈</note>. If indeed it is there, then it is good for all hours. But if they were all in the second division from Aries and **Taurus** <note>♉</note>, it will be good to focus on all matters. And if they were in the 11th [house], then that will be better for all. And if they were in the 3rd... **Leo** <note>♌</note> and **Libra** <note>♎</note>... that hour is bad for acting on other matters. In the 12th [house], if they were there, it is the worst of all. In these matters, let them consider all the hours of the day.

In the night, however, I consider that hour for doing good; then seek the first sign in the day as held above. Take degree by degree and the points in the Moon up to the degree and points in the Sun. Then you shall give points in the second place, and then the degree and points; if it were in masculine signs, then it shall be known from the east during the day; in the night, however, it is known from the **Tail** <note>term: Tail (cauda); the "South Node" of the Moon, an astronomical point where the Moon's orbit crosses the ecliptic, often associated with loss or "draining" influences</note>. Give therefore 30 to the east and 30 to the rest. Give then to the other parts, and where the sum ends, there is the not good and bad hour for doing or acting. And know in truth the second hour is good and bad, and such as it is then, all the celestial bodies shall be in days and nights, in day and night, in day.

<margin>On theft</margin>

If you wish to know if a thing has been stolen from you: [look to] the sign which will be in the east then, whether it be in your house or outside. And look at where the **Lord of the Ascendant** <note>term: Lord of the Ascendant; the planet that rules the zodiac sign rising on the eastern horizon at the moment the question is asked</note> is located. If it were in the 10th [house], then it is in its own midst. Unless it is outside of you, it is a theft, and the thief himself is there with it. And if it is not there, then it is outside. Know also if it is in the same house from which it departed before you. If it is in the 8th degree, then it is there in the eastern part; if indeed it is in the 4th, then it is in your house and is before you, even if it will be in your western part.

<margin>Another method on the same, or if you wish to know concerning a thing whether it be in the house or outside; and where the thing itself may be; and where it goes; and whether one is before the thing or not.</margin>

Lo, if it departed from you concerning some master or business, so that you may know who is strong and what concerns this, also do not forget. Observe the hour and the day; if it were in the 10th [house], then see if the business opens then in those hours. If it were so, there is merit in the business. Know also if this action is for the master in the business and consider the hour that business is undertaken. Calculate which hour of day and night falls roughly in the 10th; then look to that business. Look in the 9th [house]; if then the hour is in the house... the 10th, then the thing and the business rejoice with the man. Let it fall, and if it were so, it shall be again; and if moreover it were not in the 10th, let him take it likewise; so let it be said at last. And do thus for the other hours. ¶ And ¶

<margin>¶</margin>

If you wish to know concerning theft if sins were involved, it is observable; if it be in its own house, it were so; and then it is in the 1st, 4th, 7th, or 10th [houses] <note>note: These are the "Angular" houses, the four most powerful positions in an astrological chart, indicating the matter is prominent and "at home."</note>. Thus also the 1st sign in the Ascendant, if it fell from 4 degrees of the east. Thus if it were in the Midheaven or the Tail, it proceeds into the 2nd. It shall not proceed... and if it were in the 1st, it shall be in the 3rd, it proceeds. Namely, if it were a man, let it be the same then.

<margin>¶</margin>

If indeed you wish to know if the stolen items were red or another color, it will be clear that if that hour were then good, and if they were the sign... namely from lead or its lowest part. Concerning the signs... it will be white garments and silver or anything white. And if they were in the 2nd [house], let it be of red or dark brown [brunette]; and if it were in the 3rd, it will be in gold, and a garment of woven gold, or a golden color, etc. And if it were in the 4th, let it be of linen or a clean cloth and other painted items and ornaments. If it were in the 5th, for acting with strong seeds; as it may be certain, in **children** <note>original: "liberis"; in 5th-house astrology, this term almost always refers to offspring or procreation</note> or concerning the fruits in trees. If it were in the 6th, it is in an evil region; it may be that it is in hiding... and other beasts, or also in other vessels it was offered thereafter; and from here truly concerning the names of these things which they indicate.

<margin>¶</margin>

For if concerning a theft, at which hour it is to be known, look to whether that region is the east... and if the sign were there, he does not have it. And if they were in that sign, then he who did this will be found soon. And if it be first by itself... in the 2nd, then truly it holds its own form until the end. And if the Sun is at the end, the form is said to be at the end, and let the needle be on a new day... placed there for all the signs of nations, and the agent makes his body for a part. In the Moon, it signifies a small man with straight eyes and something red in the eye, a very large beard, and a white spot on the face; a spot for you, if then similar, then I say: **watch out!** and if the Moon were waxing, Saturn signifies a large man, and so forth.

# Whether a City is to be Captured

If anyone asks by chance or by design whether a city is to be captured, look to the sign of that city and the **Lord of the question** <note>term: Lord of the question (dominus quaestionis); the planet that rules the astrological house associated with the subject being asked about</note>. If the Lord of that city is ill-placed and harmful planets occupy the angles of the city’s sign <note>The "angles" are the 1st, 4th, 7th, and 10th houses, considered the most powerful points in a chart</note>, and if a harmful planet is in aspect with the Lord, it shall be captured. If the Lord is strong and fortunate in the head of the question, and the sign of the city is prominent in the question as described, and the **Lord of the Ascendant** <note>term: Lord of the Ascendant (dominus ascendentis); the planet ruling the sign rising on the eastern horizon, representing the person asking the question or the attacker</note> and the Moon are poorly placed, it shall be captured. 

If the sign of the Ascendant is fortunate, and the Lord of the Ascendant is fortunate along with the **Middle of Heaven** <note>term: Middle of Heaven (medium coeli); the highest point in the chart, representing success and authority</note>, and if any planet is in the Ascendant or the 12th house in aspect, it shall be captured. If a strong planet is in the sign of the Ascendant, it is a great sign. If the Lord of the Ascendant is fortunate, he shall capture it. If the Lord of the 6th, 8th, or 12th houses are in the Ascendant, the city is captured. 

If the Lord of the Ascendant is in one of the angles and is fortunate, the city is captured. If it is in a **cadent house** <note>term: cadent house (domo lapsa); houses 3, 6, 9, and 12, which were considered weak or "falling away" from the angles</note> and unfortunate, the members of the city shall be cast out or die by infirmity. If the Lord of the 2nd, 3rd, or 8th house is for the city's military, and a fortunate planet is in any angle, they have power in those angles. Likewise, if they all go out from their city of their own accord, and if a planet is found in the Ascendant, a battle will occur in the city. When the Moon is with the Lord of the Ascendant in the Ascendant, it is for the city. From the 3rd and 9th houses, if the Lord was poorly placed, there will be burning and destruction in the house and sedition, and the sign shall be terrified. If the Lord of the Ascendant is with the Lord of the 10th house, he who captures the city is given power. If there are many planets in the angles, it signifies the success of both the city and the conquerors; but the Moon must be guided to see which is favored. These are the remaining testimonies of the city according to **John of Seville** <note>original: "h hyppalenis"; referring to Johannes Hispalensis, a prolific 12th-century translator of Arabic astrological and astronomical texts into Latin</note>.

***

The **signifier of a robber** <note>term: signifier (significator); the planet representing the person or thing in question</note> is the planet present at the time... [the thief] shall be hanged by the sign which is spoken of as follows. 

From the variety of the signs, it is seen that:
**Mars** being present gives eyes that are piercing <note>unclear: sociada/infiz</note>, a face that is red or of a mixed color. 
**Venus** gives "watery" or shining eyes and is joyful; she gives a beautiful nose, a mark on the face or lip, thick lips, long hair, and makes one a lover.
**Mercury** makes the face lean and thin, and gives eyes that move everywhere; he gives beautiful lips and a swift gait.

<margin>Concerning theft</margin>
If by chance someone has this question regarding fruit or goods not found, if the Lord of the 2nd house is in the 1st, the stolen thing will be restored or returned voluntarily. If the Lord of the 8th is in one of the angles, it signifies the thief. If it is in the cadent houses, the thief has fled. 

Concerning theft, if you wish to know if the thief is a man or not: if the sign is masculine, it is a man. If the Lord of the 2nd is in the 4th, the thief is a relative or someone from the household. If the Moon is in the 4th from the Sun, the thief will be caught. If the Lord of the 2nd house stands in the 1st, the thief shall not merit to keep the goods. If the Moon stands under the rays of the Sun, the thief is hidden. If the Lord of the 6th is in the 9th, it signifies a thief from a distance. But if the Lord of the 6th is with the Lord of the 1st, the thief is known to the owner. If the Lord of the 6th stands in the 1st, the thief is a servant or a laborer. If the thief has fled to a village, he shall return the stolen goods of his own accord. 

If the Lord of the Ascendant is in an angle and sees the 8th house, it means the person from the village has not left that place with the stolen goods. If the Lord is in the cadent houses, they shall be hidden; if in the angles, he is still in the village.
