<margin>Method</margin>
When the "Year of the World" <note>term: Year of the World (annus mundi); a major astrological cycle used to predict world events and seasonal changes</note> with the Master [calculation point]... is finished, one must see to which proper **Lord Jupiter** <note>original: ". 4 ."</note> belongs, and which planet is the **Lord of the Term** <note>term: Term; a specific sub-division of a zodiac sign ruled by a particular planet</note> that Jupiter makes. Observe how it aspects the Lord of the **Sun**, which is currently in its **fall** <note>term: Fall (casus); a position in the zodiac where a planet's influence is weakened</note>, and determine how much of its own nature they ought to have. From that time when the portions are calculated, it will affect everyone concerning the matters of the month.

<margin>Method</margin>
If a question appears regarding a **deposit** <note>meaning: something left in another person's care or trust</note> and the term is broken, I can say this: if the **Lord Jupiter** was designated as the Lord in its fall, the deposit will be freely recovered. Likewise, if the **Lord Saturn** <note>original: ". z ."</note> and **Mercury** were with "our Father" <note>likely referring to the Sun or a specific angular house</note>, or if Saturn was in the first or second house, the person will not want to return the items that were deposited. If the **Lord Saturn** was present at that time, the deposit is retained. If the **Lord Saturn** was always in that same house, he will not recover them, as I have known from experience. If they are entirely unconquered <note>original: "inuicte"</note>, they go with the "physician" <note>gloss: Mercury is often termed the "physician" or "healer" in alchemical and astrological texts</note> toward the adversary, and the term shall be recoverable.

<margin>Method</margin>
To know the future of the aforesaid matter, consider the unconquered **Lord Saturn and the Sun** with the physician [Mercury] in the second house. Therefore, he says that he brings out another "net" in the same house about which he is interrogated; however, I understand this by means of the objects... [specifically] the Dog [star/constellation?].

<margin>Method</margin>
To understand a **theft**, if one has been committed, look to the Lord of the second house. It will denote the thief's path from the father, or his return, or the land... and the likeness of the vowels of the highest Lord. Likewise, look at the **Significator** <note>term: Significator; the planet representing the thief or the stolen object</note>, the aspect, and the Lord:
- If the Lord is in the first syllable of the name, the letter is **A**.
- If the Lord is in the middle syllable of the name, the letter is **E**.
- If the Lord is in the last syllable of the name, [the letter is the corresponding vowel]. <note>This refers to an old divinatory practice of using planetary positions to guess the name of a thief by matching planets to specific vowels.</note>

**Note** that regarding a "house," if two aspects look into it, then that planet is the prince. Based on the **Lord of Exaltation** <note>term: Exaltation; a sign where a planet's influence is exceptionally strong</note>, let the highest Lord at the time of the earth look at what they aspect. He is the Lord; therefore, the "good" of the Lord in all these aforesaid terms ought to participate with the Lord of the aspect in his personal joy. If he is found in an **angle** <note>term: Angle; the 1st, 4th, 7th, or 10th houses, which are the most powerful points in a chart</note>, it indicates the property is held and carried away unconquered.

**Note** that in a question, if there are two Significators—one signifying the **querent** <note>term: Querent; the person asking the question</note> which is in contention, and the other signifying the **thing sought**—and the querent comes in a double capacity... one is the significator and the other is the "instant" created by the star. It is not he who operates; and if it is had from the waters, he will pronounce... Work for the effect upon the man and not for the operation. And although some say that if it was Mercury as the physician... or according to Saturn, he himself will obstruct the measure of the Lord... in this case, the Lord is not the significator of the querent, but the "Lord of the Lord" [the planet ruling the significator]. Likewise, if by the work that was performed, such a thing is found from which one must begin; in that case, **Saturn** acts on the part of the proper deed and not the first... and concerning the strengths and the medicines...

In the beginning of any **nativity** <note>term: Nativity; a birth chart or the study of a person's life based on their birth time</note>, the first things to be inspected are:
- The **Ascendant** <note>term: Ascendant; the sign rising on the eastern horizon at birth, representing the person's body and life</note> and its Lord.
- The place of the **Moon** and its Lord.
- The place of the **Sun** and its Lord.
And other things which must be inspected for all works under the Lord of similar signs. If you wish to receive "good" through the Ascendant of the native:
- For matters of faith or travel, look to the **9th house**.
- For worldly status or honors, look to the **10th house**.
- For marriage, look to the Ascendant's relation to the **7th house**.
- For enemies, it is sufficient to look in the **12th house**.
- For death or inheritance, look to the **Lord of the 8th**.
- For the "multitude" [ancestors or hidden things], look to the **Lord of the 4th**.
- For war, look to the **1st house**.
- For procreation, look to the **Lord of the 2nd**.
- For the enemies of one's friends, look to the **Lord of the 6th**.
- If taking medicine, look to the **Moon** and the **Lord of the 4th**, and the Lord of the last house.
We must adapt the place of the Moon because it is the mediator between the upper world and the lower world, and it demonstrates to the native what happens to the man. Therefore, make your prediction clearer when the Moon is in a good place and with a "good star" [a fortunate planet]. Even if the Moon is with a "bad star" [a malefic], if the goal is evil, giving strength to the bad star is actually "good" for that purpose.

<meta>This page continues the technical instructions for "elections"—the astrological practice of choosing the most auspicious time to begin a specific activity. While the previous page focused on recovering lost goods, this page provides a comprehensive guide for various social, professional, and personal endeavors based on the "Terms" and "Aspects" of the planets.</meta>

<margin>In the **Term** of **Jupiter**, in a right or left **aspect** with **Saturn**, power is given.</margin>
In the **Term** <note>term: a 5–7 degree subdivision of a zodiac sign ruled by a specific planet, used to fine-tune predictions</note> of **Jupiter**, in a right or left **aspect** <note>aspect: the geometric angle between two planets, believed to dictate how their energies interact</note> with **Saturn**, it is a good time for matters regarding mills, farmers, laborers, and lords of inheritance. It is favorable for renting lands, building foundations and houses, digging wells and springs, and buying beasts of burden. It is good for securing estates and possessions to pass down to one's children, for hunting for hidden things, for traveling upon the sea (that is, sailing), for planting trees, and for performing or confirming divine rituals. For all these things to be granted, the aspect must be right or left, in **conjunction** or **opposition** <note>opposition: an aspect of 180 degrees, often considered difficult but powerful</note>—the aspect of **Jupiter** with **Saturn**.

<margin>In the **Term** of **Mars**, in a right or left **aspect** with **Jupiter**, it is powerful and laudable to do all good works and speak with bishops.</margin>
In the **Term** of **Mars**, in a right or left **aspect** with **Jupiter**, at that time it is good and laudable to perform all manner of good works. It is a time to speak with bishops, wise men, priors, and men of great honesty. It is favorable for seeking knowledge, doctrine, and the law of the empire, for issuing decrees, for granting the commands of the law, and for preparing legal documents and testaments. It is auspicious for endowing an inheritance, accompanying kings, seeking favors from nobles, moving from place to place, and receiving benefits from rulers and merchants. All these things are most strongly owed when **Jupiter** is in a right or left **aspect**, or in **opposition**, with **Mars**.

<margin>In the **Term** of **Saturn**, in a right or left **aspect** with **Mars**, it is good for war and hair.</margin>
In the **Term** of **Saturn**, in a right or left **aspect** with **Mars**, at that time it is good to mediate in wars, to cut one's hair, to fight in battles, to choose princes and warriors, and to fortify castles. It is the time for military service, for organizing cattle and soldiers, for engaging the enemy, and for buying weapons of war and beasts of burden. It is a time to defend the truth and to fortify strongholds and baths, etc. It is also good for visiting the sick and curing wounds, pains, and infirmities. Speak to princes then if you wish to ask something of them. This grace is granted in **conjunction**, **opposition**, or in a right or left **aspect** of **Mars** with **Saturn**.

<margin>In the **Term** of the **Sun**, in a right or left **aspect** with the **Sun**, all royal works are handled.</margin>
In the **Term** of the **Sun**, when it is in a right or left **aspect**, it is good to handle all royal works in the first place: to seek princedoms, powers, and dignities, and to acquire wealth and treasures. It is a time to treat of good character, to tend to horses and beasts, and to buy royal animals. It is favorable for speaking to princes, barons, nobles, and great men to ask for favors and to receive benefits, princedoms, and lordships. It is a time to be adorned with ornaments, to choose leaders and princes, and to earn a renowned name. It is also a time for moving from place to place. All these things may be granted in other aspects as well.

<margin>In the **Term** of **Venus**, in a right or left **aspect**, **Venus** is good for women.</margin>
In the **Term** of **Venus**, it is good for matters concerning women: seeking their affection and unions with them, adorning oneself with all manner of ornaments, and wearing new clothes. It is a time for buying gold and silver jewelry and women's finery. It is a season for joy and gladness, for visiting children, for making agreements, and for gathering with a multitude of kinsmen or wives. It is good for buying young maidservants, for delighting in wines and in pleasant places, for entering the bath, and for cutting hair. It is also a time for <unclear>darkening</unclear> <note>likely referring to hair dye or cosmetics</note> and for seeking domestic help. Marriage is favored by the aspects of **Venus**.

<margin>In the **Term** of **Mercury**, in a right or left **aspect**, **Mercury** is good for writing.</margin>
In the **Term** of **Mercury**, in a right or left **aspect**, it is good and laudable to deal with writings, to write documents and privileges, and to speak with scribes and merchants. It is a time to provide for reading and for study, to teach others the knowledge and doctrine of arithmetic, geometry, and medicine. It is a time for buying and selling, for making wise provisions, for calculating debts and recovering them, for binding agreements, and for observing pacts. It is favorable for all books and sciences, and for practicing both the liberal and mechanical arts. All the aforementioned things are more strictly required in the other aspects of **Mercury**.

It is said that when the **Moon** travels from the beginning of **Aries** <note>original: "capite cant̄" - likely a scribal error for 'capite arietis'</note> to the end of **Sagittarius**, one should buy and sell cheaply. From the beginning of **Sagittarius** to the end of **Pisces**, the influence is <unclear>different</unclear>. At the end of the year, when the **Sun** is in the autumnal months, there is great heat. When the Sun is in its <note>term: 'revolutio' - its return to a specific point</note> it returns to its midday position. This is according to **Almasor** <note>term: Almasor (also Almansor); referring to the "Centiloquium," a famous collection of 100 astrological aphorisms popular in the Middle Ages</note>.

If the planets are separated from a fortunate one and are not joined to an evil one, the day is said to be entirely praiseworthy. However, if the Moon is "void of course" <note>term: void of course; a period when the Moon makes no more aspects before changing signs, often considered a time when "nothing will come" of an action</note>, it is not good except for things like taking a bath or removing things. 

Furthermore, when the lines of influence are received by the planets, if the planets are fortunate, the day is praiseworthy; if the planets are evil, the day must be avoided. If the Moon is in its "joy" <note>note: a specific zodiac sign where a planet's influence is said to be most comfortable</note> and far from the "burning" rays <note>term: combust; when a planet is so close to the Sun that its power is "burnt up" and weakened</note>, it is a good sign. Understand these qualities of the Moon well, as its position in conjunction or opposition to the Sun determines the outcome of your work.

Observe all the modes of the Lord <term>Lord; the planet that "rules" a specific zodiac sign or house</term> of the question. If the planet that has dignity in the Ascendant is in the house of the matter <note>the specific astrological house related to the question, e.g., the 2nd for money, 7th for marriage</note>, it will be the Indicator of the thought itself.

If the Lord of the Ascendant is the Indicator of all things, the hour of the question would be the reason for the Indicator, whether the matter is good or bad. If the Indicator appears in that same place, say it shall be so. Always look for the Lord of the house and the Lord of the hour.

<meta>This page continues the technical application of astrology to medical practice by William the Englishman. Having established his credentials and the authority of the Tables of Marseilles, he now provides a detailed mapping (known as melothesia) of how the planets and zodiac signs govern specific organs, humors, and diseases in the human body.</meta>

Since the members of the body are the means by which the judgment of **Brahma** <note>original: "Bzme"; likely referring to an Eastern astronomical authority cited in medieval texts</note> is applied, one must use these principles. And further, the same author uses the humors <note>original: "colera"; refers to the four bodily fluids—blood, phlegm, yellow bile, and black bile—that were thought to determine health</note>, but if they are endowed with a superior power, they must be investigated by physicians so that the hatred of diseases may be avoided through the strength of the body as it ought to be. Therefore, the text originally composed in the first place states that the human body consists of certain **dwellings** <term>domicilia: "houses" or anatomical regions assigned to specific celestial bodies</term>.

### Chapter 3

♄ <note>Saturn</note> In the human body, Saturn rules the right ear, the spleen, and the black bile <term>melancholia: the humor associated with the earth element, often linked to depression or coldness</term>, along with both coldness and dryness. Its indicators are the sense of touch, the pulse, and various types of fevers. 
<margin>at times</margin> The diseases it governs are chronic illnesses: those of the spleen, podagra <term>podagraphic: relating to gout, specifically in the feet</term>, the resolution of limbs through the lingering of a disease, leprosy, and cancer; these are types which proceed from a cold nature.

♃ <note>Jupiter</note> <margin>♃</margin> Jupiter has dominion over the breath <note>original: "lactis", likely "spiritus" or "halitus"</note>, the lungs, the ribs, the cartilage, and the sperm along with the blood. Its diseases are the primary ones: pneumonia, pleurisy, apoplexy <term>apoplexy: a sudden loss of consciousness, similar to a stroke</term>, spasms, headaches, lethargy <term>litargia: a state of sluggishness or coma-like sleep</term>, and heart ailments; these often manifest with odors through the chest.

♂ <note>Mars</note> <margin>♂</margin> Mars has dominion over the lower parts, specifically the yellow bile, the kidneys, the veins, the testicles, and whatever is white. It also rules the liver along with the onset of diseases, namely: tertian fevers <term>fevers that recur every third day</term>, and those causing empyema <term>a collection of pus in a body cavity</term>, erysipelas <term>erisfpila: a bacterial skin infection known as "St. Anthony's Fire"</term>, miscarriages, and wasting of the lungs.

☉ <note>Sol</note> <margin>☉</margin> The Sun rules the brain, the marrow, and sight, specifically in the right eye. Its diseases are hot and dry, including types of leprosy; it also governs the sense of smell and the spirit of the spine along with the vertebrae of the spine, the buttocks, the loins, and the private parts.

♀ <note>Venus</note> <margin>♀</margin> Venus rules the womb and the saliva along with the spine, and it signifies the small of the back. Its diseases are foul and stinking: those of the liver and heart, abscesses, fistulas, and an abundance of humors, especially pertaining to the genitals.

☿ <note>Mercury</note> <margin>☿</margin> Mercury rules eloquence, deliberation, and memory; it signifies the face and the root of the tongue. Its diseases are: mental alienation <term>metfphatw: likely "metaphrenesis" or mental disturbance</term>, mania, melancholy, the "falling sickness" <term>epilepsy</term>, and phrenitis <term>inflammation of the brain</term>, along with spasms and other things that proceed from an abundance of windiness.

☽ <note>Luna</note> <margin>☽</margin> The Moon rules the left eye, the stomach, the breasts, and the female genitalia, participating in all things as the primary cause of diseases. Its diseases are paralysis, distortions of the face, the "disease of love" <term>mrbic amord: lovesickness, considered a clinical condition</term>, and those things which proceed from a fullness of humors.

And note that while it is said that all these things signify the infirmities of the body, they also signify the states of adolescence, old age, and the manifestation of death. For the significations of the planets are not changed by that voice, but they adopt various qualities according to their location and the nature of the signs they occupy.

<margin>1 Aries... 2 Taurus... 3 Gemini... these are the Dwellings</margin>
The **dwellings** of the human body are distributed in imitation of the natural disposition of the stars:

1. **Aries** <note>original: "Asentia"</note> rules the head with the face, the eyes, the ears, the brain, and the odors of the nose.
2. **Taurus** <note>original: "Domi"</note> rules the neck and the blood, along with the glands and things that hang there, such as abscesses and phthisis <term>ptifmia: a wasting disease, usually tuberculosis</term>.
3. **Gemini** rules the humors along with the milk of the breasts, the hands, and the arms.
4. **Cancer** rules the breath through the lungs, the diaphragm, and the spleen.
4. **Leo** <note>The OCR repeats '4' and uses 'Soin' for Leo</note> rules the stomach, the liver, and all things that involve the digestion of food.
5. **Virgo** <note>The OCR uses 'vuae'</note> rules the intestines and the heart.

7. **Scorpio** <note>The OCR uses 'Lia'</note> rules from the navel down to the thighs, including the kidneys and loins.
8. **Sagittarius** <note>The OCR uses 'Sio'</note> rules the private parts, the genitals, the marrow of the spine with the anus, and the heart, governing ulcers, tenesmus <term>tenasmo: the feeling of needing to evacuate the bowels</term>, strangury <term>ystragnzia: painful, drop-by-drop urination</term>, hemorrhoids, and stones.
9. **Capricorn** <note>The OCR uses 'fag'</note> rules the upper part of the thighs.
10. **Aquarius** <note>The OCR uses 'Cap'</note> rules the lower parts and the knees.
11. **Pisces** <note>The OCR uses 'Aq'</note> rules from the shins to the ankles.
12. **Feet** <note>The OCR uses 'pm'</note> occupy the feet.

Note that the more honors <term>dignitates: "dignities," or the various ways a planet gains strength by its position</term> a planet possesses, the more it is considered a "leader" or ruler. ### Chapter 6

<margin>The differences of the signs — there are three, and 5 dignities</margin>
Here [we follow] the same **Alcabitius**. Know that **Masha'allah** <note>original: "messehallach"; an 8th-century Persian-Jewish astrologer</note>, and those after Christ, composed books concerning the investigators of the heart and the investigation of hidden things, and especially because this involves the path of the stars moved in a place of mutual change. The position of a body [planet] in a foreign place may produce an effect of fortune or misfortune. In the daily motion of the world, a thing cannot be moved into another unless it is willed; therefore they are given lordships according to ten dignities. 

The effective dignities are four: 
1. The **House** <note>original: "Domum"</note>, which has the first priority.
2. The **Term** <note>original: "tm"</note>.
3. The **Triplicity** <note>original: "tgen"</note>.
4. The **Face** or **Decan** <note>original: "decan"</note>.

The Moon rules the path of the **Part of Fortune** <note>original: "pte for"</note> and its love. When several dignities are obtained in the same place, that planet is the ruler, as taught by the masters. With the first four powers added together: the House counts as 5, the Exaltation as 4, the Triplicity as 3, the Term as 2, and the Decan as 1. The planet having the most strength in this order is the principal ruler. If a planet has more powers, it is greater than its lord; if fewer, it is inferior.

The order of the 12 parts: 
The 1st obtains the most power, then the 11th, then the 10th (over the house), then the 9th, 8th, 7th, 6th, and the 4th. In this way, the eighth is second, the second is second, and the first is first <note>This refers to the "accidental dignity" or strength of the astrological houses</note>. These are to be chosen as the rulers because they suffer or enjoy all these powers.

<margin>♎</margin> When [Saturn] <note>The text likely refers to Saturn as the primary planet being discussed first in each sign, as it was considered the "greatest" of the wandering stars</note> is in **Libra** under the rays, it creates an unchanging state by its nature. When it is in its **evening setting** <term>evening setting (vespertine)</term> <note>Visible in the west after sunset</note>, it causes an inequality of the air; in its **morning rising** <term>morning rising (matutine)</term> <note>Visible in the east before sunrise</note>, it brings cold and its own winds. During its stationary points, it offers thunder and fevers for a month, as well as pits <note>original: "lacunas," likely referring to stagnant pools or hollows in the ground</note> and whirlwinds. **Jupiter** <note>original: "amor," likely a corruption of "Ammon," a name for Jupiter</note> in Libra under the rays approaches with a good complexion <note>In medieval medicine, a "complexion" refers to the balance of the four humors: blood, phlegm, yellow bile, and black bile</note>; in the evening, it causes weakness; in the morning rising, it expels infirmity; and in the stationary points, it establishes and strengthens the complexion. **Mars** <note>original: "ventos," perhaps a corruption of "Mavors," an archaic name for Mars</note> in Libra under the rays causes a state of dryness; in the evening, it is rainy; in the morning rising, it signals thunder; and in the stationary points, it is dry. **Venus** <note>original: "Benus"</note> in Libra under the rays is moist; in the evening, it is spotted <note>original: "gutonata," likely referring to a speckled appearance of the sky or skin</note>; in the morning rising, it brings sweetness to families. **Mercury** <note>original: "mici" or "me"</note> in Libra under the rays brings fortunes and its own winds; in Pisces in the evening, it is spotted; in the morning rising, it brings <unclear>ohimmes</unclear> and destruction <gloss>winds</gloss>.

<margin>♏ m r</margin> When [Saturn] is in **Scorpio** under the rays, it makes the air cold. In the evening, it also brings destruction; in the morning rising, it brings cold winds and frosts; in the stationary points, it creates dark days. **Jupiter** in Scorpio under the rays signals cold rain; in the evening, a good complexion; in the morning rising, it offers a good season and a wide measure; in the stationary points, it brings restlessness and infirmity. When **Mars** <insert>and the morning winds</insert> is in Scorpio under the rays, it causes inequality; in the evening and morning, it offers winds; and in the stationary points, it offers thunder, decay, and lightning. **Venus** in Scorpio under the rays brings rain; in the evening, it is sickly; in the morning rising, it is much more rainy. **Mercury** in Scorpio under the rays is temperate; in the evening, it is without rain; in the morning rising, it is rainy.

<margin>♐ x</margin> When [Saturn] is in **Sagittarius** under the rays, it first signals an unchanging state. In the evening, it brings sweetness and dryness; in the morning rising, it brings coldness through ice. In the stationary points, it creates <note>original: "barbas," literally "beards," referring to the trailing tails of comets or specific meteorological phenomena</note> unchangeably. **Jupiter** in Sagittarius under the rays brings good joys; in the evening, it sends rain; in the morning rising, it belongs to the elderly; in the stationary points, it signals signs from the earth. **Mercury** in Sagittarius under the rays is in humidity and humility; in the evening, it leads to infirmity and pestilence; in the morning rising, it moves the measurer greatly; in the stationary points, it brings forth temperate and mixed weather. **Venus** in Sagittarius under the rays is rainy; in the evening, it proceeds fiercely; in the morning rising, it signals good joy. **Mercury** in Sagittarius under the rays signals much rain; in the evening, it is in humidity; and in the morning rising, it signals good joy and effective action.

<margin>♑</margin> When [Saturn] is in **Capricorn** under the rays, it creates Northern winds with dark air. In the evening, coldness; in the morning rising, cold precedes it; in the stationary points, it signals dark days. **Jupiter** in Capricorn under the rays makes the air somewhat sharp; in the evening, rain; in the morning rising, it signals inequality and <unclear>fete[m]</unclear>; in the stationary points, it brings water and cold. **Mercury** in Capricorn under the rays acts in many ways; in the evening, good joy; in the morning rising, it makes for winter days and cold places; in the stationary points, inequality and fevers. **Venus** in Capricorn under the rays is thrice-frozen; in the evening, fierce; in the morning rising, rainy. **Mercury** in Capricorn under the rays is always rainy.

<margin>♒ m r</margin> When [Saturn] is in **Aquarius** under the rays, it creates two winters; in the evening, it is rainy at the beginning; in the morning rising, rain and budding seeds; in the stationary points, it flourishes with moss <note>original: "muosos," possibly referring to mold or damp growth</note>, clouds, and ice. **Jupiter** in Aquarius under the rays brings good joy; in the evening, it multiplies things and expels infirmities; in the stationary points, it offers rain and much water. **Mercury** in Aquarius under the rays brings dryness; in the evening, departing winds; in the morning rising, a bounty of movement; in the stationary points, they are a danger at sea. **Venus** in Aquarius under the rays is cloudy; in the evening, warm and windy; in the morning rising, rainy and foggy. **Mercury** in Aquarius under the rays is mossy and cold in the evening.

<margin>♓ x</margin> When [Saturn] is in **Pisces** under the rays, it is mossy; in the evening, rainy and turbulent; in the morning rising, rainy; in the morning rising, good joy; in the stationary points, it signals inequality. **Jupiter** in Pisces under the rays offers increase; in the evening, good joy; in the morning rising, inequality at sea. **Mercury** in Pisces in the stationary points signals good rain for the earth; Mercury in Pisces under the rays offers variety; in the evening, dryness; in the morning rising, lightning and thunder; in the stationary points, it signals an inequality of the weather. **Venus** in Pisces under the rays brings cold weather; in the evening, water; in the morning rising, good joy, and it makes for <unclear>fete[m]</unclear> in the sea. **Mercury** in Pisces under the rays tempers diseases and is rainy; in the evening, it signals good joy; in the morning rising, it shows a "most maritime" <note>original: "thalissimum," from the Greek "thalassa" for sea</note> joy of the heart. <gloss>Here ends</gloss> Haly de Hybe <note>original: "haby de hybe," likely referring to the 11th-century Arabic astrologer Haly Abenragel or a similar authority</note>.

<meta>The previous page concluded a chapter on planetary hours. This page begins a new formal treatise, the Breviloquium by Bartholomew of Parma, dated 1286. It transitions from technical calculations to a foundational introduction to the definitions of astronomy and astrology, beginning with a classic Aristotelian invocation.</meta>

# † Here begins the short treatise of Master Bartholomew, of the Parmese nation, compiled and completed at Bologna 
## for the prudent men of San Giorgio in Astronomy, at the request of Lord Tedisio de' Fieschi <note>A member of the powerful Fieschi family of Genoa; his relative would become Pope Adrian V.</note>, in the year of our Lord 1286.

<margin>
What is called astronomy and astrology, and from where the names astronomy or astrology are derived.
</margin>

As the Philosopher <note>The standard medieval title for Aristotle.</note> says in the first book of the *Metaphysics*, "all men by nature desire to know." This is evident from their delight in the senses. Humans, through their nature and skill, gain knowledge via experience—as stated in the first book of the *Metaphysics*, etc.—and through experience they create art, and through art they create science. Experience is the result of chance, whereas art is what is described in the first book of the *Metaphysics*. This science itself desires the <term>liberal arts</term> <note>The core curriculum of medieval universities, consisting of the trivium (language arts) and quadrivium (mathematical arts).</note>, which are likely six or seven: namely, logic, rhetoric, music, arithmetic, geometry, and astronomy. All of these take their names from the nature of the discourse itself. 

Regarding those things we intend to speak of here at present: a difference is stated between **Astronomy** and **Astrology**. **Astronomy** is called the natural science of the stars of heaven—namely, the law or rule by which a traveler is taught to know the movements of the firmament and the <term>fixed stars</term> <note>Stars that appear to stay in fixed patterns (constellations) relative to one another.</note> regarding their locations, as well as the <term>erratic stars</term> <note>original: "stellarum erraticarum"; these are the planets, which "wander" across the background of fixed stars.</note> and their movements in degrees and signs, and according to the spaces of the ether, both of the fixed stars and the wandering ones, and the part in which they rise or set, etc., just like the rising of the sun and the day. It is named from *nomos* in Greek, which means "law," and *astron*, which is "star"; hence it is called the "law of the stars." 

For as it is said in the first book of *On the Heavens* <note>Aristotle's *De Caelo*.</note>, in its primary matter, all things at the earliest morning, day, and night, are said to be in the first place of heaven, as if in the first house of the work. Nor do those which fall in the setting wish to be in the seventh place of heaven, as if in the seventh <term>house</term> <note>One of the twelve divisions of the astrological chart.</note>. And as the stars rise, they send their influence to the world in the east. In this way, their nature and the nature of those things which travel the orbit are seen according to that part. But there are those things that stand out otherwise, as is evident through the movement to a degree and sign of the stars rising and setting, and their movement from one part to another. Likewise, it is evident through a star raised from the east; we see the star at a <term>cardinal point</term> <note>The four most powerful points in an astrological chart: the Ascendant, Descendant, Midheaven, and Imum Coeli.</note>, and whether it is in the heaven itself or outside the planets, it is as they say: in heaven it is always in its own world, and it makes itself manifest the whole day, even in the west, in one and the same state. For they do not exchange with one another, nor do they change through generation, preservation, and corruption <note>Bartholomew is referencing the Aristotelian idea that the celestial spheres are incorruptible and unchanging, unlike the earthly realm.</note>. Truly, "astronomy" comes from *astro* (star) and *nomos* (law); it is the law or rule of the stars.

**Astrology** is called the science of discourse about the stars. It is named from *logos* (discourse) and *astron* (star). Thus, astrology is the discourse and greater source regarding the stars. This exists in two ways: the "natural" part, which is certain and stands by itself, and the "false" part. Truth is then defined within astrology. It does not speak only of the art; it is said that just as a man is not "bald" unless he lacks hair on his head, an astronomer must measure points by his own principles and know the technical works—to know the movement of the firmament, their space, the revolution of the signs, and the sign at any time, as is done with the **astrolabe** <note>A sophisticated portable instrument used by astronomers to solve problems relating to time and the position of the sun and stars.</note>. The name is both Greek and Latin, for *logos* is Greek, explained in the Latin tongue. Thus, the astrologer is one who, through the notable rules of this art, knows the firmament of the fixed stars, the images <note>constellations</note>, and the planets. It is necessary for other men to know the world through him regarding any sign. I ask that he be sought by the ignorant, and he will stretch out to them and solve questions. One goes to the astrologer, seeks his counsel, and investigates; he seeks the place of the star and planet, knows it, honors it, and understands it as it arrives in its time. 

But lest a man understand in a "rustic" <note>crude or uneducated</note> manner, he should be taught by a skilled teacher. It is clear from the aforesaid that Astronomy has only theory, while Astrology has both theory and practice in the art. It also has probable reasons and performs many things, namely through the work of the stars and planets, and it serves to teach the ignorant. This is done through <unclear>visions</unclear> and <unclear>begins</unclear>... the <term>gnomon</term> <note>The part of a sundial that casts a shadow.</note>, the <term>horoscopium</term> <note>A tool or table used to determine the hour-marker (ascendant) at a specific time.</note>, and fabulous suspicions and imaginations. I speak of these things as good according to... by the positioning of the twelve tables of the astrolabe, and it works <unclear>certain things</unclear> <unclear>that are seen</unclear>.

<summary>This page serves as the formal introduction to Bartholomew of Parma's 1286 treatise, distinguishing between Astronomy (the "law" of the stars) and Astrology (the "discourse" and practical application of stellar knowledge).</summary>
<keywords>Bartholomew of Parma, Bologna, Tedisio de' Fieschi, Aristotle, Metaphysics, astronomy, astrology, liberal arts, fixed stars, wandering stars, astrolabe, gnomon, horoscopium</keywords>

<meta>The previous page introduced Master Bartholomew of Parma and his treatise on astronomy and astrology, written in 1286. It established the distinction between the two fields, identifying astronomy as the science of celestial movements. This page continues by defining the specific components of the firmament and the practical application of astrology in daily life and "elections."</meta>

<margin>
+ The firmament at each hour of the day and night, and passing through the 2nd, 3rd, and 4th houses.
</margin>
...the firmament at each hour of the day and night, passing through the 2nd, 3rd, and 4th <gloss>as if they were the first, middle, and last</gloss> <note>original: "tanquam p m n" (prima, media, novissima)</note> intervals of time. It moves above that which is seen to guide its hour through the world; for the world is the firmament moving through those 2nd, 3rd, and 4th parts. This composition of the rising and setting of the signs is completed by the stars—both fixed and wandering—their motion, and their exaltation through their positions above the signs and planets in every part of the sky. This encompasses the earth and everything above the earth, the magnitude of the heavens through the sphere, and furthermore the quantity of the stars and the manner of one compared to another, through the length and latitude of the firmament.

Likewise, through this, there is a great distinction between a **star**, a **sign**, an **image** <note>In this context, "image" refers to a constellation.</note>, and a **planet**. 

A **star** is a twofold radiating point positioned in a part of the firmament of heaven, extending toward the western part. 

A **sign** <note>Referring to a Sign of the Zodiac.</note> is a large star or a great multitude of stars comprising the day-and-night part of the firmament; you shall understand it as 30 degrees in length and 12 degrees in latitude. Length in the firmament is from the east to the west; latitude is measured across the earth from the north to the south. 

An **image** <note>A constellation.</note> is a certain sign composed of many stars outside the order of the 12 signs of the Zodiac, through which the sun and all the planets move. 

A **planet** is a body of maximum splendor and motion, partaking in light and radiating among the evening stars; such bodies are like <term>comets</term> <note>Bartholomew uses "comet" here likely to describe the "hairy" or "trailing" appearance of light, rather than just the modern definition of a comet.</note> which are bounded toward the earth and are crowned at their centers. 

There are five logical points regarding quantity in the firmament and those things which are eclipsed. Many of these serve a final wisdom: namely, the points where they rise and set are called the **two gates of heaven**, because the stars and planets enter and exit through them just as people pass through the gates of any city. 

The other 8 parts are called **cardines** <note>The "pivots" or "angles" of an astrological chart: the Ascendant, Descendant, Midheaven, and Imum Coeli.</note> and boundaries. Through these, the state of the day, midday, and the years is made clear through the rising and the setting. And so, in this changeable and natural state, men are made knowing or ignorant. These offices of the long-lasting world are described here. 

When malice is strong and the weak or the widow are loathed—oh, you lovers who pass by, seeing yourselves and not seeing, or speaking and not speaking—in the case of heirs, testimony shall be given, whether good or bad. Furthermore, it pertains to locations: some are bad for the aforementioned reasons. And when one exposes themselves to these five things, the **horoscope** <note>The "Ascendant" or the sign rising on the eastern horizon at a specific moment.</note> is known. It is this which teaches a person about their entry into the world: to easily recognize the hour of the sun and the unequal days and nights. 

The aforesaid fourth part is the **Ascendant** <note>The "rising" point.</note>; when the planets are attributed to the highest points presented in that place and in the four signs, there is that which is ascending and that which is descending. There are 8 in the angles of heaven and 8 in the angles of the earth, which act according to the signs and planets. These are the joined centers that signify three dimensions; they wander from many points and have the power to wander through all things, like a prince seeking the beginning and the end. 

Through the planets in signs, one may seek the good or the bad: 
* **Concerning a Request:** Whether you will find a lover in such a place; what kind they are and if they can be had; and concerning a hidden or lost thing to be found. 
* **Concerning a Petition:** Whether such a woman loves such a man; whether she wishes to remain in such a place, or if it is better to change locations, and when; whether to wear clothes of a certain color. 
* **Concerning a Venture:** Whether someone in this generation is seen through the aforementioned planets to be suited for the task; whether they will have children; whether they will have a certain prize or a final lover; and whether such a body will be healed or die from this infirmity. 

Because the first part of all these things in <term>elections</term> <note>Astrological "elections" are the practice of choosing the most auspicious moment to begin an undertaking.</note> concerns the rising sign for the business at hand, everything in the world and in the choice of good planetary aspects depends on that part. This appears in two ways: through spiritual matters and through real utility concerning the body. In the appearance of these things, three superstitions <note>Here used in the sense of "over-standing" or governing influences.</note> dispose of the world's wealth and high status. These are taken from the earth and from above the earth, and they govern the appearance of great superfluity in the business presented, so that fortune may turn toward all men. For a thing begun is known to have good assistance on one side and bad on the other.

<meta>This page continues the classification of the sciences related to the heavens and the earth, moving from the definitions of astronomy and astrology into the "mythological" sciences, alchemy, and the various branches of divination. It identifies the legendary founders of these arts and concludes with a prayerful exaltation of God's creation.</meta>

Following this, and as part of the aforementioned, there is the **mythological science** <note>original: "fabulosa sciencia"; this refers to the study of myths and allegories as a way to understand spiritual truths.</note>. This is the science that teaches every truth through the likeness of the poets' fables, by which the different spirits and all the signs of heaven are known through divine inspiration. It covers the lands and the arrangement of figures for the perpetual memory of those things which had been in the deserts. 

The description of this science is that which teaches the fates and the mastery of metals and stones. Truly, it is difficult to escape from the brief manuals of Lavater <note>Likely a reference to an author of a lapidary or alchemical text.</note> concerning the spheres of knowledge and the sacrifices made with one’s own honors, which occur through ascension. For at the 18th hour, and through the planet of that day and night, in that place and time, the dogma of the heavens and earth is revealed.

This science is that which teaches the intellect to apprehend much of spirituality through the elements and spirits. These spirits are like the wind moving over the water and the light of the earth, through which the spirits of the water act so that man may apprehend the elegance and the infinity of God and the abyss of hidden things. These teachings are, without doubt, as thousands upon the earth, and each element is spoken of... from the earth to the moon, and from the moon to the sun. It speaks of the arts of the planets and the parts of the firmament from the rising of the sun to its setting—praise the Lord and the signs! 

And furthermore, it speaks of how the firmament is held in its love through "quadrature" <note>An astrological aspect where planets are 90 degrees apart.</note>, through the "trinity" <note>The trine aspect, 120 degrees apart.</note>, and through the signs. It shows in which part the firmament revolves, and toward which part of the heaven the stars move, and the certain spirits. It denotes the art and the strong gathering of those who love the work and the necessities required by men. It moves the power of time and divine communion, through which, from their habitations, signs are given concerning the triple sea, the air, and the earth. It provides information on notable signs in many waters. And in a hundred hopeful ways, it elevates itself through two motions, by which declarations are made in the mountains as to which planet of heaven rules which day, and which stars truly govern at that same time. Through these aforementioned intentions, one may compose the "Great and the Small" <note>Likely referring to the *Major* and *Minor* astronomical tables or keys.</note> before the dead of night.

<margin>
**Alchemy**
</margin>

Another science, without delay or artifice, is called **alchemy**. This name is known among all peoples as the art that teaches the lower or higher transformations of men. It is called the "lower astronomy," for just as the former treats the celestial things, this treats the terrestrial. It responds more through deeds than through words; the highest is public, while the terrestrial is private. This science has its origin from above, through the earth, and much is said of it. In this, the masters and teachers are Ham <note>original: "Cham"; the son of Noah, often cited in the Middle Ages as the inventor of alchemy and magic.</note>, Nimrod, Abraham, Atlas the Giant, Ptolemy, Hermes <note>Hermes Trismegistus.</note>, Mashallah <note>original: "Messechalla"; an 8th-century Persian Jewish astrologer.</note>, Sahl <note>original: "Zael"; Sahl ibn Bishr, a famous astrologer.</note>, and Haly <note>Haly Abenragel.</note>. These are the great ones, for all is said to be written through the experience of works and the joining of teachers who are dedicated to this subtle art. 

Under this science of the art of the stars, many branches shine forth, such as:
*   **Pyromancy** <note>Divination by fire.</note>
*   **Hydromancy** <note>Divination by water.</note>
*   **Geomancy** <note>Divination by earth/markings on the ground.</note>
*   **Spatomancy** <note>Divination by shoulder blades of animals.</note>
*   **Chiromancy** <note>original: "syromancia su zromatia"; palm reading.</note>
*   **Augury** <note>original: "auguromancia"; divination by the flight of birds.</note>
*   **Teratomancy** <note>original: "terntomancia"; divination by portents or "monsters."</note>
*   **Onomancy** <note>original: "obmanacia"; divination by names.</note>

*   **Sortilege** <note>Divination by casting lots.</note>

<gloss>and</gloss> These permitted things respond to the purity of this preface to God and virtue in general and in particular, concerning the manner and form of understanding these arts—how a man may do them by himself. Through a miraculous intimacy of hidden boundaries, one can, through the doctrine of proportions and the chapters of works, achieve the aforementioned effect. This is explained from above throughout the length of the land in this brief book by **Bartholomew of Bologna**, addressed to the present Lord Theodoric of Fusto, who was of Genoa.

> Glorious and worthy is God, who performs great wonders, as the prophet says. Regarding the **seven planets**, it is their order and not their mere form that acts as the governor of our "palace" <note>original: "palaciu[m] n[ost]r[u]m"; a metaphor for the created world or the human environment.</note>. Neither my own mind nor the delay of those things which pertain to its very adornment belong to itself, but rather to the governor. Just as through their order in the world, all things were rendered through creation, the governor of the right way led them here with order. They have called this very governing principle the <term>idea</term> <note>original: "ydea"; referring to the Platonic concept of a perfect formal pattern or archetype.</note>, placing it in the third sphere. Some might mistakenly think it is not from God, or that every body here is your god without a seed; but within it, the leader intends for it to be induced, and does not separate it from the moving forms in their revolution.

<margin>The planets</margin>
The form, however, is a perfect roundness, similar in its circularity to the **likeness of a ball used in a game** <note>original: "istar pile ludi"; a common medieval comparison of the spherical heavens to a sports ball.</note>. Therefore, the form is generated from truth; otherwise, it might have been serpentine or possessed other shapes and figures. Just as an acorn before it is dried, or as something rooted in a serpentine state, it is carried through the generations. Afterward, surely, labor would certainly tire to its own defect. The labor of scholars and the movement of the elements regarding their reduction in quantity makes it so that many things remain in their own properties. It makes the greatest movement of return of all movements, and from such movement, it renders its highest and sweetest sound, which is called **heavenly harmony** <note>original: "armonia celestis"</note>, or "heavenly music." 

Our own music, which is generated in motion, is called "liberal" <note>Referring to the "Liberal Arts," specifically the Quadrivium.</note>. This name, as it is found, was given by **Pythagoras** the philosopher. He discovered it from the nature of percussion—specifically from hammers striking an anvil at a glowing point. The blacksmith then understood the sounds of the hammers through their motion and their weight. From this comes the beginning of all knowledge of sound and the sound of the planets. 

And let it be known that such a music of the **firmament** or "celestial music" is named through the art of the Muses. The art pertains to the sorrowful and tearful world, yet the sweet touch of the planets is the music of pure art. Therefore, in these songs of the world, it is necessary to give the organs of love, even the right sounds and the personification of sound which are sent to serve—as a prevailing Catholic influence of the provinces. 

Indeed, so sweet and so suave is the melody of the revolution of the heavens that there is no man living in the world strong enough to be able to hear those blessed voices of the sweetly sounding celestial spheres. If one began to hear them, the movement of the firmament would conquer the soul along with the spirit, and it would hardly be preserved within the body. Only in that place is there always joy; there are three things: it shall always be in delight in the kingdom, and always with such sounds, the hearts of those in the world are joined with truth. But concerning the sky of the firmament: that which holds it up so it does not fall upon the earth is a matter of suspension; it ought not to be supported by any physical thing.

<margin>The firmament</margin>
The sky is driven forward... this is the <term>firmament</term>. It is not a web between the middle of the universe or the sky and the earth; the firmament does not sit substantially upon some other material that supports it, such as a cord or a "chain of thunder" as some have said. Rather, it stands and hangs beyond the earth by the perfect command of the sound of God's glory and His wisdom, which built it. It cannot be seized by the elements from on high, but it pertains to the heavens. Truly, the firmament of heaven is founded upon its own stability, and He founded it upon the waters, most powerful is the sky. Therefore, it is the most vast of the elements and things composed of elements. And it should be known that what is called the "eye of the world" is nothing other than what can be apprehended by human cognition. The Greeks call this <term>thohu and bohu</term> <note>These are Hebrew terms from Genesis 1:2: "Tohu wa-bohu," usually translated as "formless and empty" or "chaos."</note>, that is, darkness and truth... emptiness, as the Apostle well says in his Epistle:

But let us speak of the two **poles** <note>original: "tramontanis"; literally "across the mountains," used here to refer to the celestial poles or the North Stars.</note>...

### 83

<margin>In these names throughout, these are said to be the names of the planets in another manner from the Hebrew land. <note>original: "de terra hebrayca"; the author is providing Hebrew-derived names for the planets, though some are corrupted through Latin transcription.</note></margin>

**Daday** <note>original: "Daday"; likely a corruption of the Hebrew *Shabbatai*.</note> is **Saturn** / **Ledea** <note>original: "Ledea"; likely *Tzedek*.</note> is **Jupiter** / **Madum** <note>original: "Madum"; Hebrew *Ma'adim*.</note> is **Mars** / **Hamar** <note>original: "Hamar"; Hebrew *Hammah*.</note> is the **Sun** / **Mega** <note>original: "Mega"; likely *Nogah*.</note> is **Venus** / **Sechaph** <note>original: "Sechaph"; likely *Kokhav*.</note> is **Mercury** / **Labna** <note>original: "Labna"; Hebrew *Levanah*.</note> is the **Moon** / **Asia** is **Earth** / **Asia** is also **Earth**.

**Zachariel** is of **Saturn** / **Tzadkiel** is of **Jupiter** / **Samahel** is of **Mars** / **Raphael** is of the **Sun** / **Anael** is of **Venus** / **Michael** is of **Mercury** / **Gabriel** is of the **Moon**.

And how the hour is marked in the <term>mastery of Astronomy</term> <note>At this time, "astronomy" and "astrology" were often used interchangeably to mean the science of the stars.</note>, the planets bring forth and effect things in the individual celestial bodies. Many things are to be worked by the elements, and all things look toward some utility through the <term>ascending signs</term> <note>The "Ascendant" or the sign rising on the eastern horizon.</note> according to grace through desires, and a praiseworthy fortune through the <term>Mid-heaven</term> <note>original: "medium caeli"; the highest point the sun reaches in the sky, representing one's career or public life.</note>. And without that same grace in this sign, the angels, etc.

And because the whole firmament cuts the figure of images and signs into the face of a human, these signs are said to be virtuous for flowing influence downwards and not upwards, because it is difficult for a point to be submitted in respect to a human. And divisions [are] generations and forms, and the power of anything higher in respect [to it] is called **Natural**. And they are the disposition of the figure, seen to be through an aspect <note>A specific angular relationship between two planets.</note> according to the likeness of whatever face is sustained and moved. Therefore, a point of proportion [is used] to choose the good and avoid the evil. I grasp the good by special grace, just as you may do for others in abundance, as in the case of negotiating well for the same goods: buying a soul to profit in the land of <unclear>sight</unclear>, or planting trees. 

The **Moon** should exist in a "well-disposed" state, that is, in a good sign, having good aspects of the planets in itself. And if it is marked otherwise in the contrary, that is his business. Since there are signs in respect to the higher [realms] and an image of others and a figure of someone, others are said, etc., and others indeed in the degrees, the same and through themselves. All these are said to signify higher things. Just as the movement of man himself signifies in all things, yet it signifies other things as well, as is clear regarding the **Sun**. Although it illuminates every place of the earth, its utility illuminates others [differently], which is from the power of heat and from other institutions regarding the face, and you should note such things in this way, etc. By another means it is spoken of by hours, another by days, another by washing, another by cleansing, another for the future, another for the regular. What ought to be seen in this discourse for a desired business—the genuine receipt might produce the same effect with the help of God and the influence of the stars and planets in this star, because lower bodies are ruled by it, as the "Superior Body" says, etc.

Regarding the motion of the firmament in the signs through the whole world: the **12 Signs** have "heads," through which some of them become "straight ascensions" and others "crooked."

<margin>These are the treatises where it is discussed what occurs through the ascending signs.</margin>

Since the firmament naturally has the same motion, and that motion is its own as the body truly perceives by points; and yet since there are 12 signs, their "heads" are in the whole western part, then one will rise, and so on until the end. Their "head" does not behave that way at the entry of that hour through the end. Thus it is clear that the whole firmament makes its revolution from the east to the west every day. 

Twelve [signs]: 6 are said to be **crooked** <note>original: "tortuosa"; also known as signs of short ascension.</note> through their path—that is, 6 ascend crookedly like sheep. And 6 ascend **straight** <note>original: "recte"; signs of long ascension.</note> like a lance or a spear. The "crooked" ascension of the signs are those from the head of **Pisces** to **Cancer**. The remaining ones are from **Cancer** even to the head of **Pisces**. And those that are crooked in such signs ascend in less than 20 degrees from the horizon... through their path in ascension in time and more in 20 degrees. 

[By these] the ascent and descent of all signs in every distance of the earth [are known], since many are present in their **climates** <note>Geographical zones of the earth used in ancient and medieval maps.</note>. And concerning this ascent and descent, it is clear in the **Table of Temperament**. Just as through the days, months, and year, since the water itself has different climates through which it recurs through regions by itself; and if it expands to others and greater crookedness for the remaining signs. Therefore, as it is falsely said, it signifies nevertheless many things to be noted in its significance; namely, here the bad [signify] the motion and conformity. The planets hold various motions. In the same way it is said to the one asking in this sign and in that, as explained in the previously mentioned rubrics of this chapter. To say that if anyone asks you concerning one "head"... and the whole work, all things and the point of health and the atomic point; where **Gemini** wants something else, so that the whole earth may be open to these—namely, through such a thing from the opposite middle in the East, and from the opposite West in the South, and from the South the opposite East, and from the East the South nevertheless, etc., and it leads out the whole part which received the firmament.

⸸ Just as in the beginning of the world, the first principles of movement and the standing of others, which points are **elliptical**, are produced from a mutual relationship; just as two wheels run on one axle, which provides testimony to the power. Hence, the axle which is in the middle, around which the wheels revolve, is held as one standing principle. In all points, there is one star in the aspect of the aforementioned [pole], the mistress of all others, which is called the **North Star** <note>original: "tramontana"; the Pole Star, used for navigation.</note>, which is one of the **Great Bear** <note>original: "b'z'a maior"; Ursa Major.</note>; through another, it is called the Lesser [Bear] <note>Ursa Minor.</note>. It is in the track of the pole like a hen <note>The author likely refers to the "Hen and Chicks," a common medieval name for the Pleiades, or a specific mechanical metaphor for the celestial axis.</note>, where this point is three-sided—that is, one point is sharp and the other is wide. And in the wheel of the **firmament**, it revolves and drives the wheel of the world, which revolves between the **two waters**, the superior and the inferior <note>A reference to Genesis 1:7, where God divided the waters under the firmament from the waters above the firmament.</note>, by which the firmament of the wheel revolves in the revolutions of the planets. It is seen in the time of the planets, as it seems to have a entry into the signs from the east, beginning its turning from the west. **Heaven** likewise, according to the 19th chapter of Genesis <note>The text likely means a different theological source or a specific commentary on Genesis.</note>, is proved in the whole of the **astrolabe** <note>A handheld instrument used by astronomers and navigators to measure the inclined position of a celestial body.</note> and in the wheel of the Moon.

**C**aelum <note>Heaven or The Sky.</note> is a **round essence**, encompassing all public corporal and spiritual creations. From the Earth and other things, it is hidden from the matter of the four **elements** <note>The four classical elements: Earth, Water, Air, Fire.</note>. It is governed in a changing way. It is called the <term>firmament</term> <note>The "fixed" sphere of the stars.</note> from the beginning of the world; however, it is never perceived by the movements of the fallible senses, nor seen except through the substance of the firmament appearing to us, not in its true color, but as a **blue** <note>original: "blauūs"; an early term for blue or azure.</note> color from the high air. That quality which the common people call "heaven" is understood as an act that is not spiritual, but a graduated thing, not previously seen by us as a material essence that does not have the elements. And in the form of the water, it carries the matter of the elements, and that which is formed in substance is therefore not easily seen. It is seen as intellectual, for the temporal things are seen as corporal, while the spiritual things are determined by the affinity of the matter, just as in the water of the sea, which from a distance also appears **azure**. The firmament is like a pure field, which in the substance of the firmament reflects like a cultivated field of earth, nataurally suited to receive the highest sowing of all seeds.

¶ It is affirmed that the planets are like little rods or sprouts, and the shoots proceed from the houses of the planets. **Heaven** is said to emit the efficacy of its power into the houses of the planets, which pushes the mansions toward the Earth.

¶ In the stars, all things are sown like trees, or like images, or like shoots. For heaven is the first building prepared for the earth. The stars are like the stones for building, since they are the inhabitants of the castles, or the palaces of the houses and fortresses.

They are the fields, one might say, wonderfully adorned.

¶ Which is held to be the fortune of the world. He who labors is worthy, for in his hand the multiplication occurs, and the planets sprout forth manifestly. <meta>This page continues from the previous discussion on the North Star and the mechanical poles of the universe, shifting from the celestial axis to how power is distributed among the heavenly bodies and how this influences the terrestrial phenomenon of the winds.</meta>

Some exist in positions of **dignity** <note>original: "dignitatibus"; in astrology, a planet's strength based on its position in the zodiac.</note> and are strong, while those outside such dignities are weak and others are hindered. For the same reason, a planet does not always provide the same effect in every place. From one perspective, through many rational virtues, the soul is said to extend outside the body, just as it appears concerning the power of the Lord. In His power are all things—all ideas that please Him—which are distributed throughout all bodies. These are governed by a mutual relationship, almost like provinces, where there is no other cause for their movement toward a specific goal. Since the diverse differences of the world are signified by these paths, there must be a space for all the planets. Likewise, concerning the excellence of the heavens: those things that are preeminent in that moment are derived from and depend upon His reign, according to their nature and effect. It is not possible for a body to be divided in heaven and still move. Likewise, all things in heaven are thought to be through Him: the angels of God and the souls of the departed. In heaven, they exist in the part of essence where everything is moved by the same virtue as He Himself. Thus, it is clear to us regarding the power and the center; and it is clear to us regarding the nature and properties of the **winds** themselves.

<margin>On the winds</margin>

**I**t would be a long task for anyone who wished to narrate the full variety of the winds. Many species are described based on their causes, generated from water, from earth, and from the air (though not from fire). Their variety is divided into 16 parts; some are called "winds" and others "breezes" <note>original: "uentus / ⁊ aliq̄ ūet'us"; a distinction between a strong wind and a lighter draft or vapor.</note> because they have a certain spirit in their path or course, moving toward a specific part of the world. They are driven and moved by the cause of the influence of the stars and the movement of the individual planets. Strictly speaking, a wind is a vapor driven by the agitation of the air. Of these winds, 12 are natural, stemming from the 12 ancient divisions: 4 are **cardinal** <note>The primary directions: North, South, East, and West.</note> and are like "fathers," and 8 are **lateral**, acting like "sons and grandsons." Others are called "bastards" because they are mixed and not a simple wind; a composite wind is made of two winds that blow together. Therefore, they breathe diversely across the globe. Because they blow according to the location and the quality of the wind on the earth, there is no wind in the center of the earth itself; and if a wind has no space to exit, it returns. When it is driven by powers that precede it—such as a great subterranean heat that blows differently than it does above the earth—and if it enters the twisting holes of the earth, it generates an **earthquake** in those places. 

Historically, these winds come in the spring and autumn. The winds are properly strong and wild in months like March and September. These 12 are: **Eurus** <note>East Wind</note>, **Euroauster** <note>South-East</note>, **Austro-auster**, and **Chorus** <note>North-West</note>, which descends according to the rule. **Boreas** <note>North</note>, **Vulturnus** <note>East-North-East</note>, and **Subsolanus** <note>Pure East</note> thunder through the month of April while the sun is in **Taurus**. Eurus prevails in May. These are the winds of the months. Regarding the 12 winds, where 8 are natural and 8 are "bastards," they are known by these names: **Levante** <note>East</note>, **Sirocco** <note>South-East</note>, **Ostro** <note>South</note>, **Africus** <note>South-West</note>, **Ponente** <note>West</note>, **Tramontana** <note>North</note>, and **Grego** <note>North-East</note>. When two winds are mixed, the result is called a "bastard" wind, for the cause of these bastard breathings is a whirlwind or a transverse storm. An **Aura** is a very light breeze, while a **Vento** is strong and twisting, a most powerful way of moving that shakes the earth, and at its strongest, it drives things high upward due to the conjunction of the stars at their rising.

---

<margin>substance</margin>

**T**he work of the world consists of a substance divided into a round shape, leading toward equality or roundness. From this, there are portions called the **poles**, some of which descend. All of this is the essence of the 12 elements <note>The author may be combining the 4 terrestrial elements with the 12 signs of the zodiac or celestial divisions.</note> that descend. The planets have their center in the 8 spheres. The essence is of a single species. This roundness is understood in two ways: one is the bright and vehement light, and the other is the flame. Some describe this as a light falling upon a dense body, which if it were lacking, the world would fail. There are many such things in the firmament arranged in order, which are called **Cosmos** <note>original: "cosmīce"; the ordered universe.</note>, while the exterior is **Chaos**. Inside this is the "ortho" <note>The rising or beginning.</note>, for the sun is in a specific sign where it remains highest above the horizon in the eastern part, and such a rising is daily. This is why the sun is said to be born in its total duration according to its rising. And the rising of a **comet** occurs when it descends to the horizon...

<insert>Here are explained the very names of the first celestial sphere.</insert>

Since the celestial sphere has many parts which are their names, their meanings are explained here: **Aries**, **Setides**, **Midus**, **Atria**, **Horizon**, **Orizonta**, and **Zenith**.

The explanation for these is as follows: **Aries** is the point of the rising in the east <note>In this context, the author uses "Aries" not just as a sign, but as a technical term for the eastern cardinal point.</note>; **Setides** is the setting point or the western part; **Midus** is the midday point or the meridian; the **Horizon** is the point which is seen as the boundary between those things that can be seen and those that cannot be seen due to light or height; the **Orizonta** is the point that distinguishes those things that are under the earth from those that are above the earth, and it is said to be on a flat plane; the **Zenith** is the place in the sky which is directly above the head of someone standing on the earth. The **Hemisphere** <note>original: "Emissm"</note> is half of the celestial circle above the earth and half below; the **Zone** is one part of the celestial sphere divided into four cold and hot parts. A **Pole** is a straight line from the North Star <note>original: "tramontana"</note> to the greater North Star.

<insert>Here concerning their definitions and measurements to understand their use.</insert>

**Eternity** <note>original: "Euum" / Aevum</note> is the everlasting space of time which exists in the present world; it is that which was before the world and will be after the world, without end. **Time** is a measure of movement. We consider time in relation to the **Archetypal World** <note>term: "Mundus Archetypus" — the world of divine ideas or the original pattern of creation before it was made physical.</note>, that is, the figured world that repeats.

Time is divided into many parts: the **Atom** <note>term: "Athom’" — the smallest possible unit of time in medieval calculation, not a physical particle.</note>, the **Ostentum**, the **Momentum**, the **Uncia**, the **Part**, the **Hour**, the **Day**, the **Month**, the **Quadrant**, the **Week**, the **Year**, the **Latitude of Ages**, and the **Age**. An **Atom** is the smallest moment of time, calculated as the 380th part of an **Ostentum**.

An **atom** <note>original: "athom’"; in medieval science, the smallest possible unit of time, not a physical particle</note> is the forty-seventh part of one minute of time, which is the twelfth part of one moment.
A **minute** is the sixtieth part of one hour; it contains within itself three hundred and seventy-seven atoms.
A **moment** <note>original: "momentum"</note> is the fortieth part of one hour; it contains within itself one **ostent** <note>original: "ostentum"; a unit of time equal to 1/10th of a minute</note> and the twelfth part of one moment. There is also the **carphen** <note>possibly a corruption of a fractional term</note> of 14 <insert>15</insert> minutes, which makes up a quarter part of one hour. A **moment** is the twelfth part of one hour.
An **ounce** <note>original: "uncia"</note> is the twelfth part of one pound, and an **ounce** is also a part of other things divided into twelve parts; a **pound** is a certain part of an hour; it contains in itself 20 moments.
A **part** is the fifteenth part of the firmament according to the movement of the planets; it contains 8 points, because a **point** is the tenth part of one hour, containing in itself one and a half parts.
According to another rule, a **second** is the eightieth part of one minute, which contains one sixtieth part of a second; it is the measure of 10 moments, or 8 parts of one hour, or ninety-four points of moments.
A **point** is half of any thing divided into two equal parts. A **division** <note>original: "dīssia"</note> is two parts of a thing divided, with a third part removed.
The **as** <note>original: "asis"; a Roman unit of weight</note> is a weight of one pound, which is divided into twelve parts.
A **deunx** is eleven parts of an ounce. A **dextans** <note>original: "decūx"</note> is 10 parts. A **dodrans** is the ninth part of an ounce <note>specifically 9/12 of an as</note>. A **bes** is 8 parts. A **semis** is a half, consisting of 6 points. A **quincunx** is 5 parts. A **triens** is 4 points. A **quadrans** is 3 points. A **sextans** is 2 points. A **scruple** <note>original: "scrupul’"</note> is one ounce.

An **hour** is a measure of 14 <note>unclear abbreviation</note> which divides the movement; an hour is the 12th part of one artificial day. An hour is the space of time of the movement of the quantity of the firmament, which contains points, ninety-five ostents, and twenty-two thousand five hundred and sixty atoms; and an hour is the 6th part of one measure of the movement.
A certain measure of equal points exists which is the 8th part of one day divided into 8 equal parts.
A **week** consists of days and is the 4th part of a month. A **month** in itself is a measure of the moon.
A **year** is a measure of 12 months, or three hundred and sixty-five days and 6 hours; these 6 hours in 4 years constitute one intercalary day, called the **leap day** <note>original: "Bissextil’"; referencing the doubling of the sixth day before the Kalends of March in a leap year</note>.
A **class** is one part of a thing measured in time.
A **day** is the space of the sun above the earth. A day is the clear illumination of the air from the sun's rays, and is called the measure of 24 hours of the natural day.
**Justice** <note>likely "institudo" or "justitudo"; context suggests a fixed duration or season</note> is the quantity of the year or time of the seasons. **Summer** is the reason of the time of heat. **Light** is the court that removes part of the time. Another measure is one without mode and time. **Age** is a space of time in which one lives by right, or another which is consumed by the mind or by a translator. Age is called such from "aeon," because it began from the first age.
There follows the generation of the time of many years and measures. Concerning the measurement of the miles of the whole earth, which is a certain number of miles according to the opinions of the experts.
How far it is from the earth to the parts of the firmament or the upper heavens...

---

Concerning a certain book of his which says that the whole **Earth is round** like a ball for playing <note>original: "pila ludere"</note>. It is spherical, although mountains and valleys arise in it, yet compared to the whole, these mountains and valleys are not significant. Its circumference is 14 <note>unclear unit</note> in thickness... in its circuit, according to experts, it is twenty-five thousand five hundred miles. One principal hour represents a distance that constitutes a natural day and night. This distance is multiplied by the movement of the planets relative to the firmament. From the firmament to the earth is a distance... The space of the earth is divided in the middle.
Concerning the measurement of the circles and spaces of the movement, which is one mile. But setting aside all other things, we follow only the opinion of **Alfraganus** <note>original: "alph’nga"; Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Kathir al-Farghani, a famous 9th-century astronomer</note>.
In this place, it is stated that the latitude or solidity of the earth in its circuit from the straight path is fifty-two thousand **stadia** <note>original: "stadia"; an ancient unit of distance, roughly 600 feet</note>; and it is said that fifty-five thousand miles represent the distance, and the parts are three hundred and sixty. The latitude of the earth is calculated in miles... This space of the earth is equal to the measurement of the latitude...

From this, one first asks about the names of the other circles of the **zodiac** <term>zodiacus; the "circle of animals," a belt of the heavens divided into twelve signs</term>. This is not, however, because their nature and properties are such, but because of a certain similarity. First, the sun is in **Aries** <note>the Ram</note>. And the first sign—the point—is therefore called Aries because it is a placid animal.

It is also called this because just as the ram is a placid, gentle, and mobile animal, so specifically the world is weary <note>lassa; perhaps suggesting the world waking from winter's slumber</note> and conducts itself toward each thing, and through that sign it multiplies all kinds of things and sends them from its earth. We say this because when the sun is in that sign, the earth germinate grasses, trees, flowers, and the grasses move the springs and rivers. Men are also eager to see this because then the earth covers itself with flowers, just as all animals emerge, and then also there is good hope in the season for their fruits.

**Virgo** is so called because at that time the earth is like an animal that tires, yet it brings forth every portion of time according to labor. **Libra** <note>The Scales</note> is so called because, just as the sign itself is a midpoint between times, and there are three [seasons or months], so through that sign it is said that the birth of men is in the middle. **Scorpio** is so called because it is like the animal of that name. And afterwards it recedes.
