# Names of the months according to the Latins
That is, by the months: 1. **January** / 2. **February** / 3. **March** / 4. **April** / 5. **May** / 6. **June** / 7. **July** / 8. **August** / 9. **September** / 10. **October** / 11. **November** / 12. **December**

---
->On the partitioning of the divisions of time through all kinds of calculation<-
<note>The term <term>compotus</term> (calculation) refers to the medieval science used to calculate the dates of movable feasts like Easter and the structure of the calendar.</note>
---

All things which belong to time are principally these: points, lines, <term>atoms</term> <note>the smallest theoretical unit of time in medieval science, often 1/564th of a moment</note>, moments, the point, the hour, the day, the week, the month, the change and succession of time and <unclear>the course</unclear>, the act, ages and eras, the ages and the stars of time, and the rising and extension of the sun. These exist before they are discovered by the Lord’s predecessor. Moreover, there are six types of measures. This is the progression from the atom to the moment, from the moment to the minute, from a <unclear>unit</unclear> to a point, from a point to an hour, from an hour to a quadrant <note>a quarter-day, or six hours</note>, from a quadrant to a day, from a day to a week, from a week to a month, from a month to a year, from a year to a cycle, from a cycle to a "time," from a "time" to an age, and from an age to an era. And such things in the fullness of calculation are of the world through recovery, and the <unclear>dampness</unclear> ceases in less than a moment.

**Sixty points** <note>original: ".lx. puncta sexaginta"</note>... 
**Four atoms** make one **moment**. 
**Ten moments** make one **point**. 
**Ten and a half minutes** <note>possibly meaning 1/4 of a point or a similar fraction</note> make one point. 
**Ten points** make one point <note>this likely reflects a confusion in the transcription or a specific system of "large" and "small" points</note>. 
**Fifteen points** make **one hour**, or four "gross" points. 
**Six hours** make **one quadrant** of a day <note>the quarter-day cycle</note> without the midday. 
**Four quadrants** make **one day**. 
From a **day** to a **week**, and from a **week**, **four weeks** are made into **one month**. 
**Twelve months** make **one year**. <unclear>Certain</unclear> months make **one "time,"** which is called the "change of seasons" <note>original: "vicissitudo temporum"</note>. An **age** is established, because every month has its own time. It is called "time" here because it is a time of change, in that it brings the first year into **four "times"** <note>the four seasons</note>. It is spoken of as both small and great in that division. 

And there are **four seasons**: **Spring**, **Summer**, **Autumn**, and **Winter**. And as one describes time, that is to say, the names of things, one must also address the **qualities** of the seasons regarding their simple nature: 
**Spring** is **warm and moist**. 
**Summer** is **warm and dry**. 
**Autumn** is **cold and dry**. 
**Winter** is **cold and moist**. 

And every **three months** make **one season** <note>original: "etatem"</note> of the year. And **six signs** <note>of the zodiac</note> in the months create a greater multiplicity. Within each zodiac sign there are **three "faces"** <note>the "decans," or 10-degree divisions of a sign</note>; for one sign consists of **thirty degrees**, and **ten** degrees make **one face**. 

If one asks how many months the year has, let him say **twelve**. How many days? Let him say **three hundred sixty-five days and six hours**. How many weeks? It contains **fifty-two and one extra day**. If, however, <unclear>the reckoning is made</unclear> with nine days <unclear>remaining</unclear>, it has the days of the calendar in the year. And because of the **six hours** which are left over in each year, **one day** is created, which is called the **bissextile** <note>leap year day</note> in every fourth year. 

In the **first year**, there are 365 days and 6 hours. 
In the **second year**, there are 365 days and 12 hours. 
In the **third year**, there are 365 days and 18 hours. 
And in the **fourth year**, there are **366 days**. 
This day is given to the month called **February**, because it is shorter in days than the other months, because when <unclear>the sun</unclear> stands in the firm space of two days, it can be <unclear>restored</unclear> in its habit...

Now it is said that the beauty of heaven consists in the varied positioning of the stars. <unclear>Never</unclear> is it said that the stars are poorly sown or placed without a plan, though they may poorly appear to us. They are a better arrangement than what is understood by the unlearned <note>Latin: "idiotis"; referring to those without formal training in the liberal arts</note>. I say that they themselves are an adornment. Though they are not always clearly designated to us, they are given by God, through which one truly ought to understand the limit of all precious stones. There are 12 Signs <note>the Zodiac</note> and 36 images <note>extra-zodiacal constellations</note>; among them all are 48 constellations of stars, which contain the signs and images. These reach the number of 1,022 stars, and up to 1,600 according to others, concerning which the <term>Almagest</term> <note>Ptolemy’s foundational 2nd-century work on astronomy</note> notes by way of the planets. The stars are said to be located in different parts. There are seven magnitudes of stars, with the first being of the greatest brightness and size, followed by the second magnitude, and so on. They grant great gifts of good fortune if they are well-disposed, and ill fortune if they are malicious. Through the 48 lines <note>groupings</note> they are collected and placed in the said 12 signs, which were arranged in a book by **Ptolemy**. The planets observe their order among the lower things of man; there, from their places, they are said to possess their orbits, remaining in their circles. The bodies of the stars and planets are moved and measured by their light; each simply has its own nature and property. Their office and virtue is threefold, coming from the influence of the gods or the signs, through which the stars are placed in the firmament to signify certain variations, concerning which we have certain knowledge. Therefore, through this influence, truths and judgments are perceived which were perfected. There are 12 signs through which 36 images are shaped as accidents of those 12 signs, leading to diligent care. And because such a configuration imparts various judgments, they are taken on high. Concerning these distances as they pertain to the images, they are perceived through perfect judgment. The judgments in this part of the world and the 12 signs are where the <term>parallax</term> <note>the apparent displacement of an object viewed along two different lines of sight</note> is noted among the stars related to one another. According to these reasons, the stars are in their spheres and entireties, and their dignity is shown clearly.

In this part of the world there are three hundred and twelve <note>possibly a specific calculation of degrees or groupings</note> which in all these various ways are assigned. In the divisions of the circles there are 340. It is said of the stars that there are 1022 in total. They are graduated by divine degrees or certain distributions of the earth, from an order of comparison or argument, well-linked one to another for various causes. These stars are given to us in a plural order from the higher regions. Thus the order of the 1022 stars is described:

The 1st order <note>1st magnitude stars, the brightest</note> contains 15 stars. 
The 2nd order above the first contains 44 stars. 
The 3rd order above the second contains 208 stars. 
The 4th order above the third contains 474 stars. 
The 5th order above the fourth contains 217 stars. 
The 6th order above the fifth contains 49 stars. 

In the sixth order there are stars that are like shadows, and therefore they are called "nebulous" <note>original: "umbilosas" or "vmbrosas"</note> because they rarely appear unless the air is very pure. In another part of their place, in the fifth order, there are 9 of obscure magnitude which rarely appear at night, but are present with joy. In that same order is a star which is very effective for "experiments of love" <note>referring to astrological magic or talismans used to influence emotions</note> through the conjuration of powerful spirits.

Since the stars of these images are fixed and move by a predictable logic, the knowledge of them is of great usefulness for measuring worldly affairs in a praiseworthy manner. For this reason, anyone who is curious takes an **astrolabe** <note>a complex disk-shaped tool used to solve astronomical problems</note> on a clear night to find their altitude according to our arts, or uses a **quadrant** <note>a 90-degree measuring tool</note> by day to find the altitude of the sun. Because their positions are varied—some located in the East, some in the West, some in the North, and some in the South—certain stars are located on the "rete" <note>the pierced star-map plate of an astrolabe</note> of the astrolabe. Among these are **Arcturus** <note>original: "athofilax"</note> in the Crown, **Altair** <note>original: "vultr volas"</note>, **Orion**, the **Dolphin**, and **Alpheratz** <note>original: "alphezaz"</note> near Pegasus. There is **Betelgeuse** <note>original: "algouze"</note> in Gemini. In the Leo, there is the **Heart of the Lion** <note>Regulus</note> which extends through the fields as far as Sagittarius. These stars revolve in the revolution of the firmament from East to West. They appear to all creatures, though not all are visible everywhere. Some appear on certain nights for a short time, and thus they govern the ages and seasons.

Some of these images are said to appear above the face of the atmospheric climates <note>the medieval zones of the earth</note> and portend a change in some quality of the atmosphere in that season. As the pilgrim <note>the author or a traveler</note> considers what **Ptolemy** says regarding the observation of the stars in such times: in these 48 images, it is said that spirits reside and perform the duties to which they are assigned. From these, human nature does not escape. They hold themselves near the world in legions assigned to their office. Some are there to tempt men or the souls of men; some to carry them out of their bodies to the punishments they deserve, while there are other angels who carry them to the joys of Paradise. These officiating spirits will remain preserved in the world for these acts until the end is consumed. These spirits will cease their work, returning to the light of the spirits with the rays that encompass the supreme governor. 

All the aforementioned spirits inhabit the whole firmament. Within their dwelling, there are orders: some are **wise**, others **wiser**, and others **wisest**. The same is true of their goodness, malice, strength, and weakness. It is said they are the officials and rulers governing the very bones of the world. At a certain high and prepared time, through the mathematical art <note>astrology/magic</note>, these spirits are called upon, and they take bodies from the elements and other substances. They appear beautifully through the nature of the air and the perfection of the art, moving their eyes and appearing at a great height. These are called the "moving spirits" <note>original: "agerū"</note> and such are their offices. This book, which clearly declares these things concerning the angelic power, is called the **Picatrix** <note>original: "papica"; a famous medieval book of astrological magic</note>.

### Aries
**Aries** <note>the Ram</note> is a sign of the heaven situated in the sky by nine stars. It is the daytime house of **Mars**. As it is the first mobile sign of the earth, it has 20 known and fixed stars arranged within it, which are thus certified in their stars: and from these, one is in the forehead; two in the nostrils and around the neck; four on the back; three on the belly; one is at the tip of all the feet; one in the tail, etc. And all these are the parts under that sign, oral and similar, and you will find it full and repeatable in spiritual matters. And in no small amount of time, [those born under it] are strong in their joints, and somewhat wandering; again, they are litigious, not very wise, but in all business matters they are shrewd, ingenious, and yet fearful; they often keep silent and have done harm, as such an animal in its place and time will be invincible in every desire and tempting in delight.

Aries is the first nocturnal house <note>In astrology, a "house" is a sign where a planet—in this case, Mars—possesses specific dignity or strength at night</note>. When they begin to appear in the springtime, it is favorable for the sea and for navigation across the sea; and because their appearance gives a splendid time, it is known at the end... And if it ends well and clear, it is fair weather.

# Gemini

<term>Gemini</term> <note>The Twins</note> is the house of masculine Mercury <note>In traditional astrology, Mercury rules Gemini; "masculine" refers to the sign's active, diurnal nature</note>. One appears to look toward the East and is Castor, and the other is Pollux following it—or according to others, they take delight in their position and their chests. One figure is called Zephyrus <note>The West Wind, though here associated with the constellation's appearance</note>, like a lyre-player; its body is glowing and very large. They are like two youths embracing each other. In these stars, one star is placed at the foot and in the right hand; it carries itself like the sun in one seat with the other. Another has a lyre in the left hand. Indeed, a third figure <note>Possibly referring to a specific sub-grouping of stars within the constellation</note> has nine stars in them. The arrangement is built thus: in the head it has two bright stars; in the space between the shoulders, one...

## Libra

**Libra** is the day house of **Venus**. It is the seventh sign of the ecliptic to rise and is a movable sign <note>In traditional astrology, "movable" or cardinal signs mark the beginning of the four seasons; Libra marks the autumnal equinox</note> that possesses many stars, seven of which are visible. These are arranged so that from the side of the sun where it rises, the stars are slightly distant from one another. In the third row, they follow a straight path. One of these is brighter and whiter in color... there is one especially clear, bright, and large star in each of the scales <note>original: "bilante," referring to the two pans of the balance</note>.

One conceived and born under this sign will naturally experience both fortune and misfortune within themselves. In every part of life, there is a sense of balance <note>original: "similitudinem," perhaps suggesting a symmetry of character appropriate for the scales</note> and a concern for the affairs of others. It is fitting that one born here will be a lover above all others, by virtue of love and grace. Such a person will be quickly appeased and restored to grace.

# Pisces

# The Northern Poles and the Constellations

From the rising of the heavens, many things are held and moved in truth. There are two poles designated: the **Southern Pole** <note>original: *australis*</note> and the **Northern Pole** <note>original: *septentrionalis*</note>. The Southern Pole is never seen by us, while the Northern Pole—which is called the **Tramontana** <term>Tramontana</term> <note>Literally "across the mountains," this was a common medieval and Renaissance name for the North Star (Polaris), particularly used by Mediterranean sailors who saw the star over the Alps.</note>—is always visible. It is the fixed point around which the heavens revolve.

This northern region is marked by the **Dragon** <note>The constellation Draco</note>, which lies between the two signs of the Bears. Its body is folded in coils by the will of God. This Dragon is said to have many stars, like a multitude of shimmering scales. Between these two signs [the Bears] are the coils of the other, extending from the head to the tail. These stars are noted by some as the principles of all signs.

The power of this region is felt even in the sea through the virtue of the stone called the **Calamite** <term>calannide</term> <note>The "Calamite" or lodestone is a naturally magnetized mineral. Medieval scholars believed the compass needle was physically attracted to the North Star itself.</note>. This stone has a nature that denotes the position of the Tramontana. In every navigation, the compass needle <note>original: *calamm̄a*</note> is moved by the power of the Tramontana, directing the sailors. It is a great wonder of nature that a stone has such a relationship with the heavens.

The movement of the stars around this pole is constant. If one stands with their feet firm, the Tramontana appears in its place... it is like a virgin following the planets... it is the greatest movement in the heavens...

<margin>Greatest</margin>
**The Great Bear** (Ursa Major) is an image located at the summit. It is coiled and folded, with its head near the star called the Tramontana. This image represents to us a **Wagon** <note>original: *plaustrum*; a common folk name for the Big Dipper or Ursa Major is "Charles’s Wain" or the "Wagon."</note> because it appears to roll through the sky. The **Bear-Watcher** <note>original: *filax*, likely referring to Arctophylax or Boötes</note> follows it, containing many stars. It has 5 stars in its head and 6 in its face. In total, it encompasses the pole. In its form, it has two stars in the back, two in the forelegs, and two at the ends of the feet. On its tail, by the nature of its creation, it has stars that represent its great power in the heavens. This constellation provides great confidence to those who watch the sky, for it is a magnificent sign in the orb of the world, granted honor and dignity.

**The Lesser Bear** (Ursa Minor) is an image located at the tip of the Dragon’s tail, where it is coiled. This image contains that star which is specifically called the **Tramontana** by its northern names. It is smaller than the Great Bear but is situated more directly at the southern-facing part of the northern axis. This image also represents a wagon to us, revolving around the North Star.

# Boötes

**Boötes** is a celestial image which is called **Arcturus** <note>original: *archurus*; although Arcturus is the brightest star in the constellation, in the Middle Ages, the name was often applied to the entire figure of the Herdsman.</note> by some, having many stars. Because there are 31, their position—that is, their arrangement—is thus confirmed: in the head he has one; one bright star in each of the shoulders; in the right hand four; in the left hand one; on each breast one small and somewhat dim star; on the right elbow one; one bright star on each knee, of which the middle one is large and bright; on each foot one; in the <unclear>servant</unclear> <note>original: *famulo*; this may refer to a specific part of the figure's clothing or an attendant figure often omitted in other versions.</note> thirteen, one at the point of the foot, [and one] in the middle of the staff. Furthermore, those who are conceived and born under this sign always find rest in labor, and exist more in poverty than in riches; nor do they ever care for the status of a village <note>original: *statu villam*; this suggests an indifference to social standing or rural politics.</note>. Wherefore, a person of this kind ought in all things to be compared to a poor laborer; and this is the form according to its appearance in the sky.

**A**ndromeda is a figure <note>original: *ymago*</note> that possesses many stars; there are twenty of them, and they are very visible to many people. **H**ipparchus <note>Hipparchus of Nicaea (c. 190–120 BCE), an ancient Greek astronomer whose catalogs formed the basis for much of medieval celestial knowledge</note> also confirms this. And if he preaches with humble preaching, many dangers will appear to him; through these dangers many misfortunes will arrive, always following the merits of those who are in danger; then he shall die for the sake of his own merits and good deeds. This is its form as it appears in the air <note>original: *in aere*; referring to the appearance of the constellation in the sky</note>.

**T**his present figure <note>original: *ymmago*</note> represents the one who has eighteen stars, which are visible to everyone. The arrangement <term>arrangement: *despositio*; the specific layout or mapping of stars in a constellation</term> and verification [shows that] in the head he has one good, bright star. In the right hand, one; in the right elbow, one; in the left [elbow], a bright one; in the right thigh, one; in each knee, one; and in each shin, one; in the foot itself, one; and in the cloth <note>original: *tela*; this likely refers to the *chlamys* (cloak) or the weapon held by Perseus</note>, one. **I**n the middle, as if he were conceived [under this sign], it is said that one born under this sign will be of great stature, as well as wise, talented, extravagant <note>original: *luxuriosus*; in a medieval context, this could mean both a love of luxury or a tendency toward lust</note>, benevolent, yet argumentative, unprincipled, daring, strong, and confident. It is said he will be very fortunate in possessing the temperament to achieve his desires; he will attain great riches, but he will squander many goods as if they were his own misfortunes. # The Image of the Dog or Sirius

The Dog, or Sirius, is said to have many red stars—eighteen or twenty, as the professors <note>original: *professores*; likely referring to established astronomical authorities or teachers of the quadrivium</note> say it is constructed. In the head it has one bright star; in the neck it has two, and in any such pair, one is always very small and dark; in the chest <note>original: *precordijs*; the region of the midriff or around the heart</note> it has two; in the left front foot, three; in the right hind foot, only one, which is bright; along the spine of the back, three; and because of the two at the top of the beginning <note>likely referring to the base of the neck or start of the spine</note> it has one bright star; in the left thigh, one; in the left hind foot, one; and at the tip of the tail, it contains one. It holds the natures of both the Sun and Mars. Those born under this sign will be envious, <term>tyrosus</term> <note>original: *tyrosus*; a difficult term perhaps meaning "hostile" or "prone to anger," or potentially related to the "tyrant" or "Tyrian" (proud) temperament</note>, litigious, disdainful, and loud. He will be a very faithful lover, a seeker of things harmful to others, a wanderer, and more poor than rich. He will live more in leisure than in labor, and so forth. This is the form as it appears in the sky.

# The Image of the Ship

The Ship, or Argo <note>original: *Argois*; referring to the *Argo Navis*, the mythological ship of Jason and the Argonauts</note>, is an image having many stars, of which 20 are visible. Their arrangement is according to the artist's craft: in the head of the rear mast, three; in the stern <note>original: *puppia*</note>, four well-shining ones; namely, in the tiller downward, two are seen; and some are somewhat obscure; in the prow <note>original: *prora*</note> above, three; and in the rigging, three. And there is another image which is the tortoise <note>original: *teltudo*; likely referring to the constellation Lyra, which was often depicted as a tortoise shell</note> making a sound, with two stars; it is seen obscurely and is almost invisible.

Those conceived and born under its reign will always be more poor than rich; yet they will delight in singing without complaining. They live by the light of labor upon the water, traversing many regions and maritime exchanges, providing for some and leading back others, according to the form and appearance in the heavens.

# Proteus

**Proteus**, who by another name is surely called **Sarzarine** <note>original: *sarzarine*; this name is obscure, possibly a corruption of an Arabic star name or a specific alchemical term</note>, is said to be an image of the heavens having many human aspects related in this way: since those things which are visible in our <unclear>sphere</unclear> <note>original: *nro*, likely *nostro* [mundo/celo]</note> certify almost all things, just as in our <unclear>sphere</unclear> there are two flames. In the extremities there are two <term>remedies<gloss>original: *medele*; likely referring to specific stars with perceived healing or balancing properties</gloss></term> in each of which are two points. Beneath the mouth it is <unclear>well-like</unclear>; there are two [points] below.

<insert>¶</insert> And a person conceived or born under this sign in its exaltation <note>In astrology, the "exaltation" is the position of a planet where its influence is most powerful</note>... will always delight in the experiences of love, but also in divine transmutation <note>original: *transmutacio divina*; a clear reference to alchemy, the art of changing the nature of substances</note> with a clever cause. Whence, from the grace of the constellation, he is graceful and [disposed] to inherit such things. Likewise, he is the lover and father of metals and an **alchemist**; he is a man who is as if ingenious and sagacious, yet weak in the chest, fearful, and timid. For this is its form according to its appearance in the sky.

# Centaurus

**Centaurus** is an image of the heavens <note>original: *ymago celi*; a standard term for a constellation</note> that has many stars, among which 30 are visible.

The arrangement of these stars is described thus: In the head, it has three small and dark stars. In each of the shoulders, there is one good, bright star. In the right elbow, one; in the right hand, one; one further forward; on the top of the back, two. In the belly, two; in the right loin, one good, bright star; in the tail, three. In the knees of the hindquarters, it holds two; in the curve of the shoulders <note>original: *armorum*; may refer to the junction of the human and horse parts</note>, one; and in the front feet, one.

The arrangement of the stars of the little beast <note>This refers to the constellation **Lupus** (the Wolf), which Centaurus is often depicted holding</note> which he holds in his hand is also as follows: In the head, it has two, of which one is larger and brighter than the other. In the shape of the back, two <unclear>strongly</unclear> set on either side. In the tail, two. On the tip of the left hind foot, one bright and splendid star. On the front foot, one good, bright star. Thus, therefore, the aforementioned has three [stars] in the head. 

A person born under this sign, or in its head, will be strong, bold, and eager. He will be tenacious and <term>calculating<gloss>original: *excogitatos*; someone who thinks things through or devises plans</gloss></term>, and lucky in obtaining <term>salvations<gloss>original: *salvationes*; likely meaning safety, recovery from illness, or general preservation from harm</gloss></term>. He will delight greatly in delicate foods and drinks, and in fine clothing and weapons. He will always be more rich than poor. He will be <unclear>promoted</unclear> freely over other persons and will arrive at a rank of honor and office. He will overcome his enemies, and at the end of his life, he will die a good death. He will be undefeated, kind, and of good <term>constitution<gloss>original: *renibus*; literally "kidneys," which in medieval medicine were thought to be the seat of vigor and physical strength</gloss></term>, and so forth.

This is its form as it appears above to the eyes:

# The Magpie without Horns

The **Magpie without horns** <note>original: *Pica sine cornubus*; while "Pica" usually means magpie, this likely refers to the constellation Corvus (the Raven)</note> is an image of the heavens having many stars, among which 20 are visible. 

The arrangement of these is confirmed thus: In the head, three are seen in a small **curve** <note>original: *flexura*; referring to the joints or bends in the celestial figure</note>; in the eyes, one, and it is small and dark. In the second curve, it has three; in the third curve, two; in the fourth, two; in the fifth, reaching to the tail, eight very bright ones. 

Above the mouth <note>original: *os*</note> there are two good [stars]; and on the lips, two dark ones; along each of the sides there are three; in the bottom, two; in the head, what is called a "mane" <note>original: *coma*</note>, which is very large and clear; on the back, two; upon the wings, four; in the tail, two; and on each foot, one.

One conceived or born under this sign will naturally be fortunate to have many goods, and he will retain many things. I am of the opinion that he will be rewarded, and likewise [he will be] a receiver of poverty and sadness, which will be the first of his labor. And he will be perpetually weak, unless he recognizes a benefit that might come to hand... <unclear>potentially</unclear> this is the form according to its appearance in the heaven.

# Canis, or the Lesser Dog

**Canis** or **Antecanis** <note>original: *Antecanis*; literally "Before the Dog," referring to the constellation Canis Minor and its brightest star, Procyon, which rises before Sirius (the "Dog Star").</note> is an image of the heavens having many stars, more than three that are possible <note>likely meaning "visible to the naked eye"</note>. The arrangement is confirmed thus: along the neck it has one very splendid star; in the chest, two very bright ones; along the top of both shoulders it is surrounded [by stars], since the one in the neck is thicker <note>original: *grossior*; larger or more prominent</note> than the others. 

One conceived or born under this sign is always faithful in pursuit, swift in action, yet timid like a dog; nonetheless, he is swift and **sagacious** <term>sagabundus: a medieval term for someone with a keen "scent" or sharp intuition, like a hunting dog</term>; and though he may fall from wealth to poverty, through much labor he will obtain and sustain his position, yet he will hope in God more than in his own labor. And this is the form according to its appearance in the sky.

# Equus, or the Winged Horse

**Equus** <note>original: *Equus*; the Horse, referring here to the constellation Pegasus</note> is the second image, having many stars, more than seventeen that are possible or a few visible... <note>the text here seems to omit a word or use a shorthand regarding visibility</note>. 

The arrangement is confirmed thus: on the head it has three [stars]; below the eyes and in the neck, two; in each **wing** <note>original: *ala*; this confirms the identification as Pegasus, the winged horse</note>, one; in each foot, one; and in the belly, two; in the left flank, two; in the hip and under the tail, two; in the first joint of the tail, one. 

One conceived or born under this sign is always a lover [of others]; though poor, he will arrive at grades of honor according to his dignity. He will be sagacious and will live in delicacy; at all times he will be loved by all persons. He is honest and modest, a peacemaker. For indeed this is the form according to its appearance in the heaven.

**The Eagle** <note>original: *Aquila*</note> is a heavenly image consisting of five stars, and it is spread across four parts. He who constructs it strikes at a specific point; it is like a hand holding a spear <note>original: *hastam*</note> by which, if one seizes it, he dwells within the web <note>original: *tela*; perhaps referring to a woven pattern of stars or a loom</note> and leads others. Let him mark the points of the banner <note>original: *vexilli*; a standard or flag</note>, for these are the specific things to be maintained in one's outlook. Under this sign were others of famous heart <note>original: *cordis*; implying bravery or spirit</note>, and through it, one shall arrive at such honors as befit their dignity. He will love, fear, and honor his own; thus, he will be poor in the matters of war <note>original: *pauper in bellico*; possibly meaning humble or lacking in worldly military equipment, yet spiritually strong</note> and a striker among his enemies; for indeed, he is strong in battle, a quality much to be desired in the heavens.

<meta>This page marks a transition from the astronomical figures of the previous section to a new treatise on Chiromancy (palmistry). The text shifts from celestial signs to the "natural signs" found upon the human body, specifically the lines of the hand, which were believed to correspond to the soul's health and the body's internal organs.</meta>

# Here Begins Chiromancy 120
<term>Cyromantia: Chiromancy, or the art of palmistry, derived from the Greek words for "hand" and "divination."</term>

**J**ust as the sciences are ranked among themselves, and one thing arises from other things—as is the case in the parts of metaphysics <note>original: *metaphisice*</note> concerning divine matters—so too does it begin with the nature of all things, starting from the things of God at birth. These are generated in two possible ways of demonstration. For some things exist through themselves from the beginning, namely the natural sciences, of which one is that which is called by the common name **Chiromancy**.

**C**hiromancy is the art of recognizing the manifold passions of fortune <note>In this context, "passions" refers to things that happen to a person, both good and bad.</note> within the bodies of animals through those figures which are produced by nature in the organs of the senses. And just as there are certain natural signs—for these are present by necessity or debt because we say all things are aided by persuasion—diverse influences of bodies happen by chance. Thus, as we say regarding the present, from which we speak of justice, temperance, strength, fortitude, and passions such as anger, love, and joy of this kind; likewise, whether for any other benefit, you may increase or diminish honors, etc. However, just as in a book <note>original: *biblia*; likely referring to a "book of nature" or a standard reference text</note> there are types of signs, lengths, quantities, colors, lifelike features, limits, and extensions, so it is in animals through the various organic parts of the human body, as appears principally under the quality of the earth which is the soil. And there is a division of the hands into three parts: the first part is that which is between two lines, one on each side.

**O**f the hands, however, the forearm suffices as the first part. Another part, indeed, with the mount of the thumb <note>original: *monte pollicis*; known in palmistry as the Mount of Venus</note>, is the mount of the hand and is called the **wrist-joint** <term>rasceta: the lines or crease where the hand meets the wrist</term>. The second part is called the **palm**, which begins from the wrist and the line touching the part of the mount of the thumb and ends at the roots of the fingers. The third part is the finger of the thumb and is called the index <note>The text here seems to conflate the thumb and index or describe their junction.</note>. The fourth part consists of those things regarding the thumb which have two heights from the fingers and are large in the middle of the hand. On the back of the palm, there are two middle areas which are in the hand, which are called the birth-parts at the end of the back of the hand. Another of the divisions...

**L**ines are of two types: accidental <note>original: *accidentales*</note>, which are caused by heat, cold, hunger, strength... infirmity, labor, and work, and from then on with little permanence in the mind; and natural lines <note>original: *natales*</note> from which they are immutable and always continue as points. These are the ones that follow the virtues of men, such as wisdom, and such lines end at the summit, namely, it is said of all men by which many are just as they were at birth, and such are at the insertion of the nature of the wrist.

<margin>
Line of Life
</margin>
What they are: and it terminates in the mount of God <note>original: *monta deum*</note> in the lower part which is called the Balance <note>original: *libra*</note>, and through the human soul they are feared, and it is called the "most vital." And temporally through the depth... and it is that which is elevated above the arch of the thumb and is said to be between the thumb and the index finger and terminates at the wrist of the hand. And it is a "one-hearted" line <note>original: *unochorus* (?)</note> because the line corresponds to the **heart** through the passions; it is the first line of the hands from the thumb. While the mount of the thumb is the extension of the thumb.

<margin>
Line of the Brain
</margin>
The line of the middle of the mind and body extends through the middle of the hand and is called the mount-line <note>original: *montisicet*</note>, or the line of property, or the **Triangle**. This takes its beginning from the rise of the first line between the thumb and index finger, but extends from the root to the end of the middle of the palm. And it is a "one-hearted" line because this line corresponds to the **brain** and is so called.

<margin>
Table Line or Base of the Triangle
</margin>
The **Table Line** <note>original: *linea tabularis*</note> by some, and the **Base of the Triangle**. It enters the body through the linear... and the base of those, the quantity of the triangles, and this is seen because in the hand... not the whole. And these arts admire it, and whatever those lines say...

<margin>
Line of the Liver
</margin>
...angles. And it is a "one-hearted" line because this line corresponds to the **liver** and the stomach or the spleen. And the space that is between these lines is called the **Triangle** <term>triangulus: the central plain of the palm, often called the Plain of Mars</term> in the mind of the palm. The line divides...

<margin>
Table Line, or the Summoner, or the Moral Line, or the Line of Death
</margin>
The **Table Line** <note>original: *mensalis*</note> enters the middle of the palm from one part and is called the Table because it shows the delay of the palm. And it is called the Middle Line <note>original: *linea maria*</note> of the body because of the shortness of the closure and the flexion of the fingers through the hand... and it is called the **Line of Death**. And this is when it proceeds with the middle finger towards the index. And it is a "one-hearted" line because this line corresponds to the **genital members**. That which is between the Table Line and the Middle Natural Line is called the "Table of the Hand" <note>original: *mesa manus*</note>, regarding the subtlety of the table... in the quadrant of the hands. Thirdly, that which is between the Table Line and the root of the fingers, between the movement of the fingers, is called... at the root of the fingers under the mount of the index... others in the space that remains.

...boldness of spirit and audacity, and it shows a very well-disposed heart. Furthermore, if the line is broad, colored, and glowing red, and if they possess a balanced and clean stature, it shows a person of excellent personality and a good mind. However, if it is broad but poorly colored, it signifies a heavy or serious nature—and this is to be understood uniquely of this line. 

If the line is very slender, it signifies breadth of character <note>In medieval physiognomy, a very thin line was sometimes thought to indicate a lack of focus or a "thinned out" spirit</note>. What is found in its disposition is highly prized. Conversely, a "natural line" that is poor is described as follows: first, such a line is deep, thick, trembling, and infected with an earthy color, which everywhere shows an earthy and bestial vice. But when the said line is more red than the wrist lines <note>original: *rasteca*, a variant of *rasceta*, the lines wrapping the wrist</note>, it shows a middle-ground of cruelty. 

If such a line is very luminous and somewhat twisted, it shows a deceptive nature, a lustful person, much evil, and impurity. If a line descends from that line into the very center of the "natural line," he will be wounded and will perish from the wound. If from this middle line a certain line descends toward the "natural line" in a sudden way from above, the person is submissive and fragile, and will be wounded. When the said line stands near the line of life and is near the wrist-ward face of the palm, it is of little consequence then; but if it is tempered in good color, it shows the highest goodness.

***

<margin>The Natural Middle Line</margin>
This line, which is called the "natural middle," is judged by some because it signifies the portion of the brain. If the line is straight and of good disposition, it shows goodness in the person's judgment, property, and generosity. Because this line is long and runs so that it extends through the middle of the palm of the hand, it always signifies riches and a long life.

<margin>On keeping promises</margin>
If such a line is very glowing red so that it does not exit the hollow of the hand, it shows poor, miserly, and moderately lustful people; and if they have promised anything, they will be imperfect in their promises. 

But if the aforementioned line extends toward the part of the hand opposite the middle of the pinky finger, it demonstrates people of great virtue and many immense qualities. This is also shown if it shines forth in the middle of the said finger from the opposite side. 

<margin>Long life</margin>
If this line extends into the middle mount <note>The Mount of Saturn</note> so that it does not touch the mount of the hand, it is perfect.

<margin>Right Angle</margin>

In hands that are red in due proportion to others, it is said that they possess a natural disposition and a balanced <term>complexion</term> <note>In medieval medicine, "complexion" refers to the balance of the four humors—blood, phlegm, yellow bile, and black bile—which determined a person's health and character.</note> to a high degree. And those people are such by their properties because they show derogation and greed. And as to the form, that which is designated in the middle shows many kinds of discord and reveals unknown things in the hand.

### Fingers
Fingers that are of an honest appearance in their ends are seen in many as [a sign of] sight. If the fingers are small and thin, they indicate a foolish person; if they are thick, they also indicate a foolish and wild person. Very thin fingers show fallacy, and if in the middle limit they are low <margin>to speak</margin> they show proper conversation. Those that are narrow show that grace and devotion are provided. If they are gathered together so that air does not pass through, and are much clenched, it shows a malignant nature. If the fingers are erect and bend toward the back, it indicates [a certain quality], and if they bend into the palm of the hand, [it indicates another]. If they are spread apart from each other, it shows a talkative and improper person. He who divides his fingers in many ways may be like a drum. If they are empty, it signifies communication and malice. And if he suffers this habit in the palm so that it can be absent far away, if it is within the palm he will suffer this even if it is absent. It is one thing if he extends his hand to take, and another thing when he holds the hand moderately. If he does so quickly, it is seen as a sign of a malevolent or gluttonous person who is conscious of food. If someone habitually holds the hand closed while walking, it shows an impetuous arm. And if by habit he holds the thumb closed over the other fingers, he is a greedy man.

### Nails
Broad nails that are thin at the end and shiny signify intellect in their properties. When they are very red, they indicate the best [intellect]. If they are long and narrow, it shows anxiety or coldness. If they are very small for the body, it shows greater coldness and stupidity. Nails that are [blunt] at all ends indicate malice; likewise, a pale hand <margin>malignant</margin> or rounded nails indicate a person prone to anger. It is said that if white spots are found on the nails, they signify riches and conditions; black spots show typical curses and wickedness. Generally, such nails show melancholy and arrogance.

### Color
A proper color that is clear white and red equally shows a typical goodness of genius. A red color shows the best of love; such a color is never displaced in the whole world. For where the body is white and apprehensive, over a sanguine body, the proper color is that which is not changed by summer labor or by cold. This color which we have spoken of shows strength; and clarity and smoothness in the hand are signs of a beautiful complexion because they derive from it.

As it appears in this treatise, **chiromancy** <note>original: "cyromancia" — the art of palm reading</note> is the method of demonstrating a person's nature through the perceptible signs of the hands—such as their natural death, adversity, and thus for making judgments. Contained within these lines are one's dignity, greed, poverty and misery, happiness, misfortune, discernment, grace, confidence, piety, justice, and the utility of all these things; as well as the modesty, cowardice, and audacity of a person. Thus, these perceptible signs of a person concern their birth. <unclear>of that</unclear>. It tests such things as lineage, cunning, knowledge, and wisdom. For this reason, chiromancy does not indicate "accidental" matters—such as whether one will eventually become a member of the clergy or a layman, or whether one is currently wealthy according to Christian standards—as if these were various paths to life. Rather, it assumes a "hand of knowledge," not that chiromancy should indicate what someone is *actually* doing with their hand, but rather it signifies what their *nature* ought to be according to the mapping of the hand, following the judgment of a skilled practitioner and the discretion of another. <insert>as is required, etc.</insert> Then, moving from the middle to the outer parts:

### The Degrees of the Parts of the Hand
Regarding the parts of the hand as required for this science: The part from the arm to the beginning of the palm is called the **base** <note>original: "recepta" — the wrist area where the hand is 'received' by the arm</note>. <insert>Indeed, the part from the base</insert> to the table-line is called the **palm**. And from the palm to the fingers is called the **mount of the fingers**. There are four fingers and the thumb: the **index**, the **middle**, the **medicinal finger** <note>original: "medicus" — the ring finger, traditionally associated with healing and medicine</note>, and the **ear-finger** <note>original: "auricularis" — the pinky finger</note>. The mount of the palm is divided into parts, according to which chiromancy pertains more to the palm and partly to the lines of the palm. Following the parts of the lines of the palm, we must first speak of the anatomy of the books <note>likely referring to the structural layout of the source texts</note>, through which we gain knowledge of the palm.

There are principal lines which are called the **veins of the palm**. The first is called the **line of the heart** or the **table line** <note>original: "linea cordis sive mensalis"</note>; it is said to be the most fortified extremity, stretching toward the index finger, while its other extremity is received by the little finger. Another line is called the **middle line of birth** <note>original: "media natalis" — often corresponding to the Head Line</note>, so called because it tends toward the middle of the length or the "table" of the hand. The third line, which appears less clearly, is the line called the **triangle** <note>original: "triangulus"</note>. Its two parts cover the lower angles and it moves from the base, tending through the middle of the birth-line toward a line that is sometimes flat and twin-like; some say there are three members, though often they are not found. These parts of the lines constitute the "triangle," while the other is called the right line, the left line, and the middle birth-line at the summit of the triangle. And there is a line called "outside the birth and table lines," which indicates friendship and extends through the palm to the fingers.

Let us speak now of the parts of the palm. The extremity of the hand where the arm is joined and touches the palm, where the heart line extends toward the thumb, is called the **mount of the thumb**. The area from the table line to the fingers is called the **mount of the fingers**. Thus, whatever is directly positioned under a finger is called the mount of that finger, and so on for the others in their own way. There is also another line if it appears in an angle, or if it is figured in the hand's "table" <note>the flat center of the palm</note>. If the mount of the palm in the lower part of the hand extends lengthwise as far as that distance, the two heads are divided. We speak first of the principal line, and second of the others. From this it is clear they are "general" lines, etc. The principal birth-lines are called **general lines**, and those which follow are **final lines**; for general lines are rarely found [missing], etc. They signify much in many people, whereas **accidental lines** are those which arise from labor, hunger, cold, and from those afflictions for which the art is not defined. I speak, therefore, of the general and special signs which are recognized specifically through these categories.

Second, let us speak specifically of those lines which constitute the triangle, and first of the **line of life**. I say that if the line at the summit of the root and the head is long, it signifies a long life; and if it finishes in the middle of the palm, it signifies a short life. This shortness is judged as being more or less according to the quantity received; the greater it is, the more it suggests death. Therefore it is called the line of life, because through healthy and twin-like bodies [marks] in these principal joints, if there is good strength in the whole hand—especially if it is well-colored and not too pale or overly red—then it indicates through its **physiognomy** <note>original: "fisonomiam" — the assessment of character/fate from physical features</note> that if there are two short lines not articulated in the hand, it signifies a short life. This is because a good physiognomy, according to its articulation, proceeds from a good natural internal virtue which follows the law of life. And if the line of life descends clearly and doubly to the base without distraction, through this treatise etc.

If this line is well-articulated, deep, clear, and long enough, it is a sign of a good mind. If it crosses the whole palm, it is a sign of a good mind and a superior spirit. If a good line crosses through it, it signifies a person who acts with stability.

If the line is entirely thick and red, it is a sign of rudeness and lack of foresight. If this line is deep, thick, humped, and full of red pits, it is a sign of a short life that will end in sudden death. If it is twisted and varied but of good color, it is a sign of joy. If the natural line appears pale, it is a sign of a weak complexion. When it is twisted and inconsistent, it signifies a change in one's goals or that the person is not constant in what they say. If it is not flat but pitted with many dents, it signifies deep darkness <note>original: "profunde nigrati"</note> and misfortune.

When this line is twisted and inconsistent with diverse colors and grainy in the middle, it is the sign of a man prone to theft. If lines move from it toward the **mensal line** <note>original: "mensalem" — another name for the Heart Line</note> and they are clear and of good color, it is a sign of good grace and the fulfillment of promises. If the line is broken between itself and the mensal line, it shows fidelity and a good complexion; the fewer the breaks, the more these qualities are present. From this line, a line extending to the mensal line shows friendship, whereas a crooked one shows lying and a tendency toward laziness. If it is well-spaced and has lines like hairs exiting from it, it is a sign of confidence and, especially in ministers, a sign of chastity and modesty. If it is well-balanced and small and has two lines departing from it, it is a sign of love, audacity, and good grace. If this line is very thin, pale, inconsistent, and worn, it is a sign of weakness of the body and the head.

...the **Table Line** <note>original: "linea mensalis" — the uppermost horizontal line on the palm, known today as the Heart Line</note>. It shows death through the highest father <note>likely referring to the Mount of Saturn or God</note> if it is entirely reddish and red, and if it is straight and extended through the middle. This is a sign of death through **acute fevers**; and if many lines come out from it toward the middle, it is a sign of throat ailments at the time of death. And if in that line it touches the ascending line up to the Table Line in the manner of a single sign, it shows a universality of rare ends. If it is twisted, it signifies all kinds of dangers.

If one line comes out from the Table Line, going all the way to the bottom and touching the middle, it is a sign of change and of great labors. If there are two such lines, it signifies even more dangers. If another line cuts across toward the root of the **thumb** <term>pollex | the thumb, associated in palmistry with willpower and base instincts</term>, it is a sign of immodesty. If a good line is complete and shows itself at the root, and crosses through the joints, it is a sign of good form and wealth. Many twisted lines... sign of the sublime, both present and future in the body...

But it shows if it is pale or small. A twisted and wide line... signifies theft, especially regarding women. If many lines are in the middle, it signifies friendship; it shows one more apt to fathering sons and daughters. Straight lines on the mount of the middle finger <note>the Mount of Saturn</note> show health of the womb and a wife who will be a prior <note>perhaps meaning of high status or a first wife</note>. They also show a desire to be ignited... such lines are a sign of honor and dignity. Twisted and thick lines descending from the middle line signify the sublime present and future etc.

One line predicted from the Table Line reaching to the root of the **little finger** <term>minimus digitus | the pinky, associated with communication and commerce</term>, if it is found there, shows greed in a man and chastity in a woman. If it is twisted and thick in one place, it shows gluttony, and in a woman, corruption. If there are many lines there, and one is larger than the others, it signifies honor both in life and toward women. If lines descend from the root of the little finger, they signify the sublime present and future in the knees and feet. Lines ascending from the Table Line show the sublime in the arms.

Regarding the fingers, it signifies... which crosses over... if they are descending, they indicate a hindrance. Lines found in the **Table of the Hand** <note>original: "tabula manus" — the quadrangle or space in the center of the palm between the major lines</note>... they show that a person ought to have a good world and concept... if they appear in a certain way, it is a sign of peril. These lines are not to be trusted if they disappear...

And also, lines found in the mount of the thumb signify friendship or enmity. In the middle of the thumb, it shows riches. If lines descend from the thumb toward the life line, it signifies a great firm truth. In the mount of the **index finger** <term>index | the forefinger, associated with Jupiter, ambition, and leadership</term>, it is a sign of labor in acquiring riches. If one line exits from the upper angle toward the line... it is a great indication that such a person is held in high regard. If the lines are like little coins <note>original: "moneteles"</note> tending from the thumb upward, and if they are many, they show great dangers. If they appear in the whole hand...

2. The **Life Line** <note>original: "linea vitalis"</note>. 3. Sign of... and if it appears round... in the thumb, such a person is in danger from water. If it is large and found on the hand or thumb, it is a sign of hanging.

Likewise, **Albertus** <note>Albertus Magnus (c. 1200–1280), a prolific medieval scholar who wrote on the natural sciences and whose name was often attached to chiromantic texts</note> says in his commentary on the first book of *On the Ages*:... if a finger is longer, it is a sign of greed. If it is so distinct that it can penetrate <note>perhaps meaning it can be moved independently or has deep furrows</note>, it is a sign of generosity, etc.

A hand that is less warm and too cold is a sign that the **head** <unclear>capite</unclear> is poorly disposed <note>meaning the person's mental or physical health in the head is out of balance</note>; and if the hand is well-disposed, it is moderate to the touch, which is a better disposition regarding illness. A twisted **Heart Line** <term>linea cordis | the horizontal line stretching across the top of the palm</term> above is a sign of adulterers and is notorious; and if it touches in the middle, it is such a sign as is said here: that the person is born of adultery, which is said by the judgment of the woman's [hand]. It is taken in the **left hand** for a woman and in the **right** for a man, where it is said that one ought to be very suspicious. 

Because it is not [certain] what is said regarding the hand of the woman and the left hand in the man, even if it were true; rather, one must diligently consider the signs of both hands. And if the signs of the right hand and the left hand agree with each other, then a judgment should be made for both. If the signs of both hands disagree with each other so that they are opposites, it is because the sign is stronger in the principal hand—that is, in the right rather than the left. Regarding this, they say a judgment <unclear>of sin</unclear> is captured on a **Thursday** <note>original: "die iovis" — Thursday was traditionally associated with Jupiter</note>; for the judgment of many is based on the lines. 

This I do not think should be held as certain; for others say this [person] has tendencies and dispositions equally for both the good and the evil. But if it should please the lower authorities shown in the hand, it is possible that he ought to be a **Bishop** or a **Deacon**; but rather, he himself ought to have honor according to his own status. 

And one should not judge by the aforementioned signs alone, but by many signs together. These things which have been said concerning **chiromancy** <term>chiromātia | the art of palm reading</term> shall suffice for the present.

If the **Life Line** <term>linea vite | the line that curves around the base of the thumb, traditionally associated with vitality and longevity</term> is deeply received in the **mount of the hand** <term>mons manus | the fleshy pads of the palm, each associated with a planet or physical organ</term>, it may indicate danger through bile <note>original: "fella"</note>, yet it signifies riches in the present. If the lines of the thumb are prominent in the hand, they are called the **gem** <term>gemma | also known as the rascettes or wrist lines; they were often seen as a "bracelet" of luck or health</term>, and it is profitable if they appear so. And such is the disposition of the garments <note>referring to the patterns on the skin</note> on the thumb and finger; all "buds" <note>original: "germina" | small growth-like marks</term> signify an arrival at a good order. If there are holes <note>original: "foramina"</note> or two tubercles <note>small swellings or bumps</note> and fences, it excels above others; it signifies that a woman will suffer because of her son. If the figures are reclined above as if toward a lamb, it signifies something regarding a daughter.

If the **Life Line** and the thumb are swollen from the index finger, it signifies a suffocation of the lineage... and if it is protected by hard colors with its persistence, let it be a sign of pride. If the **Liver Line** <term>linea epatis | also known as the Health Line or Mercury Line, associated with digestion and the liver</term> is taken at every degree, it provides all the dispositions of the heart toward death, and it provides many things toward a direct end. One who recognizes what strikes him sees the hand of a woman like a serpent near the stomach; and if she has these "throats" <note>likely referring to narrowings in the lines</note> and they are pale on the finger. 

However, if the lines are wide, troubled, and broken, then it signifies an infallible decrease in a new way <unclear>modo</unclear>. One who has such branches [on the lines] will endure in riches and honor. And if the end is not "tested," he is perfect in all things.

If in the middle the Life Line is tested above, it shows a sign of death. If it leads to two [marks], he will leave behind eight. If the **Head Line** is good with the **gem**, it signifies a good condition; and as much as it is long and straight, the mount of the hand will show him to be a figure of long life and great deeds. It is a sign of good disposition and boldness. If it is pale and swollen, so that he does not exercise the hand heavily, it shows a person of small faith. And if it is in the lower part, it always signifies a son; as long as the hand hangs from the palm, and if at the end it has a point touching a line that stands, he will seek the depths and it signifies a long life with boldness and honor.

If the **Liver Line** and the **Stomach Line** are long from the **gem** with color, it signifies the goodness of the liver and stomach; if it does not appear and is discontinuous, then the opposite is true. When it is doubled with tubercles, one should fear headaches and liver pain openly. In a person where it strikes with ferocity and remains in the "grain" of the hand <note>original: "granu manu" | possibly the center of the palm</note>, it signifies infirmity with the gems and difficulty. It also offers a long life and makes one very amiable and famous. From the "throat" [of the line], let it touch the **Life Line**, and the fame of the liver is raised in various ways. Because the Life Line and the Liver Line remain in the grain of the hand, which is opposite that space which is the limit and distance of the mind.

It signifies infirmity, rashness, and a tendency toward being struck. If the lines are distant, it signifies a fear of snakes. If it is arranged from the opposite half, it is a sign of good disposition, even if the distance is small and useless in speech. To a speaker in the world, it is a sign of a gift. # The Physiognomy of Aristotle Begins

<margin>
If there are spots and immediately those which guide a white man, and toward a round face and soil from the bones of the earth, toward a red color, hair, and dry humors—and here they say it is unique; it pleases the whole face or me, if they are <unclear>gloc</unclear>, it is necessary they are and clean(?)
</margin>

**In** the rest, you should know that which you must not be ignorant of: that one recognizes the soul according to its dispositions through **physiognomy** <term>physiognomia | the art of reading character from physical features</term>. The Almighty and the First [Cause] loves it, for it is most truly a habit that elevates nature. Just as humans and beasts do not have the same disposition, if a person tends toward evil, through teaching they may be led toward the good, though this is a matter of great difficulty. Because of this, it is useful for a man to act by reason, even when he finds it difficult due to the signs of temptation he carries. Men are more capable or prone to certain behaviors according to the species [of their features]. For through all things, the substances of the body are most easily purified. In the earth, there are various **complexions** <term>complexione | the balance of the four humors (blood, phlegm, yellow bile, black bile) which determines temperament</term> of men.

It is a good sign through all things to have hair that is smooth, long, or of a reddish color. Such a man has a jaw that is mobile according to his will. A person who is "clay-like" <note>original: "argillosum," likely referring to a dull, earthy skin tone associated with the melancholic humor</note> is snatched by the earth. A man with much hair on his feet is like a bird. Those of a flame-colored or fiery complexion, and especially those with much hair, particularly on the jaws, are rendered men of greed; yet they also show a good ability to learn. 

A red, wide, "iron-like" forehead full of hair is a sign of envy and ignorance. Eyes that are, as it were, equally twisted, combined with a hard forehead and "bitten" hair <note>possibly meaning jagged or unevenly growing hair</note>, are the sign of a thief and a deceiver. 

A face that is flat and round with a good color indicates a person prone to joy. Straight fingers, thin fingers, and ears extended long and outward indicate a tendency toward anger. In <unclear>...</unclear> I hold that such are of good memory. Those who possess a moderate quality in these things, and whose eyes have a certain "biting" quality along with roundness [are balanced]. Smooth and sparse hair signifies gentleness and a moderate coldness of temperament. 

Redness of the hair on the chest and on the belly declares a man who is driven by love and lust. A purple or dark color <note>original: "purpur color," likely referring to a livid or bruised-looking complexion</note> is a sign of anger and <unclear>...</unclear>. Here, large and "unclean" eyes signify a man who is ferocious, lazy, and disobedient, especially if the light of the eye is reddish. Those whose eyes decline from a moderate state toward another color and have sharp edges possess a lovable intellect and are faithful. 

Eyes that move rapidly <unclear>...</unclear> such a man is fraudulent, a thief, and unfaithful. One who is hairy <unclear>...</unclear> and looks down toward the earth is <unclear>...</unclear> and unclean. Such a person will be unstable; they say it is a sign of an evil or unhappy person. Similarly, those with a gaping mouth or <unclear>...</unclear> are of unpleasant dispositions. 

And here, a nose that is wide in the middle and turns down at the tip indicates a liar. A very large and wide mouth indicates one who is bold and a great eater. One who has firm lips and a <unclear>...</unclear> face is very greedy and unstable in other works. A small face declining toward <unclear>...</unclear> is of the worst mind; such are deceivers. A figure or person who is flat is very prone to wrath. 

A voice that is beast-like indicates <unclear>...</unclear>. A voice of moderate firmness <unclear>...</unclear> is a sign of one who is fearful. A man who speaks frequently and with much movement is "unclean" in his speech and a deceiver. A man who abstains from the movement of his hands is of good intellect, good disposition, and good profile.

In the disposition toward many arts, thickness and shortness in the fingers is a sign of shrewdness <term>calliditate | a cleverness that can lean toward cunning or craftiness</term> and a lack of refinement. That person is of the best memory and well-disposed by nature who has soft flesh, possessing a middle ground between roughness and smoothness. This should be observed not just in any place, but especially in winter—leaning toward a white complexion and a reddish chin. One should look for straight hair, and eyes of moderate size leaning toward roundness. A person with a head of moderate size and a well-proportioned neck is well-disposed; such a person carries themselves well <note>original: "humi bene declinat," suggesting a graceful or humble posture</note> and has a clear voice. They are also marked by long palms and long fingers that taper toward the tips, and a gaze that seems mixed with joy and cheerfulness.

Beware of every man who is unfortunate and irredeemable <note>original: "inebiali," likely a corruption of "emendabili" (correctable) or "inequali" (unbalanced)</note> whose limbs are mutilated; for he is to be avoided just as one avoids enemies. Flee also from every man who appears flat and lowly, for he is prone to vice and immodesty; he is boastful in his soul <note>original: "ventosam in anima," literally "windy in soul"</note> and possesses penetrating eyes and unstable steps. He who has a "bad face" <note>likely referring to a harsh or asymmetrical countenance</note> is never lacking in spirit, but it is a corrupted one.

And if these traits are found in women, a calm expression and a "frozen" or glassy appearance <note>original: "glacia," perhaps referring to a cold or staring look</note> indicates greater danger. Observe the nose and the eyes; any shameful feature or one tending toward blackness is to be feared. If the flesh is of a certain color and the eyes are not blue-grey <note>original: "glazei," a term often used for owl-like or pale grey-blue eyes</note>, such a woman is said to be corrupt.

In these writings, you must not be deceived. One must not form a judgment based on only one of these signs; rather, collect the testimony of all the signs and follow what the aforementioned rules give you. And in your judgment, always lean toward the better interpretation.

The length of the solar year—namely 365 days, 5 hours, 49 minutes, 12 seconds, 28 thirds, and 37 fourths <note>Medieval astronomers divided units into sixty parts: minutes, seconds, thirds ($1/60^{3}$), and fourths ($1/60^{4}$) for extreme precision.</note>—is always determined by the quantity in that sacred [calculation]. They wish to find through the zodiac whether it moves more over the meridian line <term>lineam meridianam | the imaginary north-south line passing through the observer's zenith</term>, and if there are the aforementioned days in the zodiac; that is, it requires the whole zodiac as 360 [degrees], namely for the 360 days of the whole weight. For there still remains 4 days, 14 hours, 49 minutes, 14 seconds, 28 thirds, and 37 fourths. Specifically, in total 21 hours, 49 minutes, and 6 seconds. And if you convert those 4 days by 24 [hours], it becomes 1201 hours. Place those 120 [hours] and multiply by 60, and it becomes 7200 minutes. Always convert the aforementioned 49 hours by 60, and it becomes 300 minutes, which you add to those 7200 previously mentioned from all 4 days, and the number becomes 11400. To these, add 49 minutes in its own quantity, and it becomes 11449 minutes. In that [calculation], divide by 360, and you have the total quantity of motion. And by that quantity, the sun may move 30 minutes more over the meridian line than the time of the previous hour. Multiply the result by 3897, then multiply by 60, and it becomes 23400. When multiplied by 2, namely by its own multiplication, it becomes 140400. By 360, the conversion demonstrates the time through the zodiac that the sun moves over the meridian line in the time of the second hour. And so you shall work until the end, until the length of the year is reduced into the motion of the day. They wish to find the length of the year through the said motion of the sun in the aforementioned day as it must be worked. In that quantity mentioned above—4 hours, 49 minutes, 12 seconds, 28 thirds, 37 fourths, 49 fifths—in that said day, it produces the following result in two parts. And if in serious turn: 18, 32, 53, 38, 10, 46, 32, 30. Namely, by which you convert 304 by 60, and multiply the results from 21600, which is the time of the day. Add the aforementioned 14 to the two, and it becomes 21614; all these in motion must be reduced: 21614 divided by 60. Multiply the result from 1216840, to which you add 32 and the aforementioned [values], and it becomes 216... and multiply the result. And so you shall work so that I may find this [calculation] of the zodiac, which is determined by the length of the year as an absolute sign. The result is <gloss>the true motion</gloss> of the sun in one day.

# The Motion of the Sun

Here is the motion of the sun <note>original: "motus solis"</note> as held by the masters through the fourth [part], because according to the **tables** <term>tables | astronomical charts used to calculate the positions of celestial bodies over time</term> I am not able to [find it], yet for a man it is difficult to begin because of the slowness of their motion in two parts; indeed, if someone should say that it ought to be encountered elsewhere in the coming [years], we are able to have this through the great masters, to whom it must be added for a greater explanation.

## On scarcity and if a star...
Look at the place, for it signifies over the oil of olives; an abundance of oil having been tasted, the King who at the exit hastens. Less so if it was in its own house. But if in the <term>house of its fall</term><note>The sign opposite its exaltation, where the planet is weakest.</note>, always there is the greatest cheapness; and in the house of its fall, there will be detriment, namely of the grain as much as it hastens.

Regarding the Keys of the Moon
</margin>

When there is an opposition in the lordship of the angles <note>The four most powerful points in a horoscope: the Ascendant, Midheaven, Descendant, and Imum Coeli.</note> of the ascendant at that time, through the latitude of the signs to the luminaries <note>The Sun and the Moon.</note> equally; and if the Lord of the opposition is in the house of the cadent signs <note>Houses 3, 6, 9, and 12, which were considered "weak" or falling away from the angles.</note>, it indicates that **rain will not fall** in all that time, nor in the greater part of that year. And if it should be in the feminine watery signs <note>Cancer, Scorpio, and Pisces.</note>, and the Lord of the sign looks upon the Earth itself, it signifies the same ratio of the nature of rain. And if there are "Almutens" <note>original: "alimtaȝ" — a planet with the most dignity or "power" over a specific degree.</note> in the ascendant, join them through conjunction; and if they are Almutens to the luminaries, then there shall be **rain even unto abundance**. And if the Sun precedes the luminaries, then the rain decreases. Look to the ascendant in which the Moon shall be, for then the rain will descend. And I say elsewhere that if the lords of this ascendant or the angles are situated thus, it signifies rain; if not, and it does not look upon them, then rain will not fall. In every matter of the aspects regarding rain, which is known by experience: know that when planets are retrograde in the signs, they bring rain. This is especially true of the inferior planets <note>Mercury and Venus.</note> when they enter feminine signs, and it is a very clear testimony if the sign is of the earthy or watery triplicity. And if it is in the sign of the "Pourer" <note>original: "effusor" — referring to Aquarius, the Water-Bearer.</note>... and it is said if the Lion <note>Leo</note> signifies the rising of water through the great sign which goes out in authority... from the part of the rising and the moisture, that is, the "carrying of water." And you should wash the luminaries in the houses... and if the Moon gives its power in its revolution, it signifies that in that month **rain shall descend**. It can also be known from the time it will descend by the distance of the Moon, which is the equal distance between the place of the Lord of the opposition and the place of the aspect. When the Moon reaches those degrees, rain will descend. It is a more certain testimony if the Moon changes its nature on that day. And here are the **Keys of the Moon**, which are found by its distance from the Sun <note>These are specific degrees of separation between the Sun and Moon used to predict weather changes.</note>: the 1st is at 12 degrees; the 2nd at 124 degrees; the 3rd at 168 degrees; then the opposition of the Sun at 180 degrees <note>The Full Moon</note>; then at 192 degrees; the 10th at 224 degrees; the 11th at 240 degrees; the 12th at 314 degrees; and the 13th at 348 degrees. These are the "Keys" proven by the ancients from experience. You must always look to the state of the retrograde planets in their houses to see if they signify rain, especially in the first house or the midheaven. And for **winds and the shaking of the earth**, these come from the conjunctions which signify winds. You must look at the month and the lords of the ascendant; if they are in signs that breathe, it signifies great winds throughout the year. If they are in watery signs, they signify rain with lightning and thunder.

### On Earthquakes

This is also perceived in the revolution of the year. For if [the planets] are in the dignity of the **earthy signs** <note>Taurus, Virgo, and Capricorn.</note> and no benevolent planet looks upon them, and the Moon is in a specific station, it signifies an **earthquake** occurring in whatever place that sign represents.

### On Wars and to Whom They Happen

We must look to the "Lord of the Year." For if the Sun has power over the ascendant in the revolution and is in an angle, it signifies **war and the shedding of blood**, especially if it is in a sign that has the form of a human <note>Human signs include Gemini, Virgo, Libra, and Aquarius.</note>. And if it is in any of the earthy signs, it signifies earthquakes or the shaking of the ground. And if the Lord of the sign is seen by a good aspect, then the judgment is lessened. And if Mars is oriental of the Sun <note>Rising before the Sun in the morning.</note> and in a human sign, it signifies wars, but the **fear and suspicion** of it will be greater than the actual shedding of blood.

If it [the planet] is above the stars that signify war, and it is in a feminine sign, it signifies... and from the signs of moisture, which are judged by the winds. If the sign is earthy, it signifies [famine] or a lack of grain. And if another planet looks upon that sign, it changes the effect. If it is in the place of the Lord or the aspect, it signifies the Lord of the house... and concerning the earthquake and the long battle... in the time when the Lord of the sign is in an earthy sign... it signifies the death of men or a scarcity of fruit... in that time...
